bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第193卷卷第一百九十三

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, fascicle 193, the one hundred ninety-third volume.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 193.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀九】　起著雍困敦九月，盡重光單閼，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 9] Beginning in the ninth month of the year Zhuyong/Kundun, ending in Chongguang/Shanyan, altogether a little more than three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 9] From the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenguan through the seventh year of Zhenguan—a span of somewhat more than three years.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，初令致仕官位在本品之上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingwu, for the first time it was ordered that the official rank of retired officials should stand above their nominal grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, the court first decreed that retired officials should hold rank above their nominal grade.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「比見群臣屢上表賀祥瑞，夫家給人足而無瑞，不害為堯、舜；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Lately I have seen the ministers repeatedly submit memorials congratulating [me] on auspicious omens. When every household is provided for and the people are content yet there are no omens, that does not prevent one from being like Yao or Shun;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Lately I have seen ministers again and again submit memorials celebrating auspicious omens. A realm can be well fed and at peace without any omens at all and still be no less the equal of Yao or Shun;

sentences.zh: 百姓愁怨而多瑞，不害為桀、紂。

translations.literal: when the common people are full of grief and resentment yet omens abound, that does not prevent one from being like Jie or Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: and a people sunk in grief and resentment may see omens multiply without ceasing to be Jie or Zhou.

sentences.zh: 後魏之世，吏焚連理木，煮白雉而食之，豈足為至治乎！」

translations.literal: In the age of Northern Wei, officials burned trees with conjoined trunks and boiled white pheasants to eat them—was that sufficient to count as the utmost in good government!"
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Wei times officials burned trees whose branches had grown together and boiled white pheasants for food—was that truly the mark of perfect rule?"

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔：「自今大瑞聽表聞，自外諸瑞，申所司而已。」

translations.literal: On the day dingwei an edict stated: "From now on, great omens may be reported by memorial; as for all other omens, report them only to the responsible office."
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he issued an edict: "Henceforth only the greatest omens may be announced by memorial; all lesser omens are to be reported to the appropriate office alone."

sentences.zh: 嘗有白鵲構巢於寢殿槐上，合歡如腰鼓，左右稱賀。

translations.literal: Once a white magpie built its nest in the locust tree by the sleeping hall, the branches intertwining like a waist drum; those at his side offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once a white magpie built a nest in the locust tree by the imperial bedchamber, its branches intertwined like a waist drum, and the attendants congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我常笑隋煬帝好祥瑞。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have often laughed at how Emperor Yang of Sui loved auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have often laughed at Emperor Yang of Sui for his obsession with omens.

sentences.zh: 瑞在得賢，此何足賀！」

translations.literal: The true omen lies in obtaining worthy men—what is there to congratulate in this!"
translations.idiomatic: The real omen is winning worthy men to service—what is there to celebrate in this?"

sentences.zh: 命毀其巢，縱鵲於野外。

translations.literal: He ordered the nest destroyed and the magpie released into the wild.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the nest torn down and the magpie released into the open country.

sentences.zh: 天少雨，中書舍人李百藥上言：「往年雖出宮人，竊聞太上皇宮及掖庭宮人，無用者尚多，豈惟虛費衣食，且陰氣鬱積，亦足致旱。」

translations.literal: Rain was scant; Zhongshu Sheren Li Baiyao submitted a memorial: "In past years palace women were released, but I have heard privately that in the Retired Emperor's palace and in the Lateral Courts there are still many women with no use for them. This not only wastes food and clothing in vain; the accumulated yin qi can also bring drought."
translations.idiomatic: Rain was scarce. Li Baiyao, a secretary in the Secretariat, memorialized: "Although palace women were released in earlier years, I hear that many still linger unused in the Retired Emperor's quarters and the inner palaces. Besides the waste of food and clothing, the pent-up yin force alone is enough to cause drought."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「婦人幽閉深宮，誠為可愍。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Women shut away deep in the palace—truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Women shut away in the deep palace are indeed to be pitied.

sentences.zh: 灑掃之餘，亦何所用，宜皆出之，任求伉儷。」

translations.literal: Beyond sweeping and dusting, of what further use are they? They should all be released and left free to seek husbands."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond sweeping and dusting, what use are they? Let them all leave and marry as they choose."

sentences.zh: 於是遣尚書左丞戴冑、給事中洹水杜正倫於掖庭西門簡出之，前後所出三千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Dai Zhou and Jishizhong Du Zhenglun of Huanshui to select them out at the west gate of the Lateral Courts; in all, more than three thousand were released before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Dai Zhou, left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and Du Zhenglun of Huanshui, a supervising secretary, to select women at the west gate of the inner palaces. More than three thousand were released in all.

sentences.zh: 己未，突厥寇邊。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, the Turks raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the Turks raided the border.

sentences.zh: 朝臣或請修古長城，發民乘堡障，上曰：「突厥災異相仍，頡利不懼而修德，暴虐滋甚，骨肉相攻，亡在朝夕。

translations.literal: Some at court asked to repair the old Long Wall and mobilize the people to man the forts and barriers. The emperor said: "The Turks have been visited by calamities and strange signs one after another. Jiali does not fear them and cultivate virtue; his cruelty grows worse daily, and his kin attack one another—his fall is a matter of morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers urged repairing the old Long Wall and drafting the people to garrison the forts. The emperor said, "The Turks have suffered one disaster after another. Jiali will not take warning and mend his ways; his cruelty grows worse, and his own kin turn on one another. His fall is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 朕方為公掃清沙漠，安用勞民遠修障塞乎！」

translations.literal: I am about to sweep the desert clean for you—why must we weary the people repairing distant barriers!"
translations.idiomatic: I am about to clear the desert for you—why weary the people building distant walls?"

sentences.zh: 壬申，以前司農卿竇靜為夏州都督。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the former Minister of Revenue Dou Jing was appointed Area Commander of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the former minister of revenue Dou Jing was made area commander of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 靜在司農，少卿趙元楷善聚斂，靜鄙之，對官屬大言曰：「隋煬帝奢侈重斂，司農非公不可；

translations.literal: While Dou was at the Ministry of Revenue, Vice Minister Zhao Yuankai was skilled at levying and amassing; Dou despised him and said loudly before the staff: "Emperor Yang of Sui was extravagant and imposed heavy taxes—the Ministry of Revenue needed a man like you;
translations.idiomatic: While Dou served as minister of revenue, his vice minister Zhao Yuankai was adept at squeezing the people, which Dou despised. He declared before the staff, "Emperor Yang of Sui was extravagant and taxed heavily—the ministry needed a man like you;

sentences.zh: 今天子節儉愛民，公何所用哉！」

translations.literal: the present Son of Heaven is frugal and loves the people—of what use are you!"
translations.idiomatic: but our present sovereign is frugal and loves the people—what use are you here?"

sentences.zh: 元楷大慚。

translations.literal: Yuankai was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 上問王珪曰：「近世為國者益不及前古，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wang Gui: "In recent times those who govern the state fall ever further short of antiquity—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wang Gui, "Why do recent rulers govern ever less well than the ancients?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「漢世尚儒術，宰相多用經術士，故風俗淳厚；

translations.literal: He replied: "In Han times Confucian learning was honored; chief ministers were mostly men versed in the classics, and so customs were pure and thick;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Han times honored Confucian learning, and chief ministers were mostly classicists, so customs stayed pure;

sentences.zh: 近世重文輕儒，參以法律，此治化之所以益衰也。」

translations.literal: in recent times literature is prized and Confucian learning slighted, with law mixed in—this is why good government and transformation grow ever weaker."
translations.idiomatic: but lately literature is prized while learning is slighted, and law is mixed in—that is why rule grows weaker."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，御史大夫參預朝政安吉襄公杜淹薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Censor-in-Chief and participant in court governance Duke Xiang of Anji, Du Yan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Du Yan, censor-in-chief and participant in governance, Duke Xiang of Anji, died.

sentences.zh: 交州都督遂安公壽以貪得罪，上以瀛州刺史盧祖尚才兼文武，廉平公直，征入朝，諭以「交趾久不得人，須卿鎮撫。」

translations.literal: The Area Commander of Jiaozhou, Duke of Sui'an Shou, was punished for greed. The emperor, considering that Lu Zushang, prefect of Yingzhou, combined civil and military talent with integrity and fairness, summoned him to court and instructed him: "Jiaozhi has long lacked the right man; I need you to pacify and govern it."
translations.idiomatic: Shou, area commander of Jiaozhou and Duke of Suian, was punished for corruption. The emperor summoned Lu Zushang, prefect of Yingzhou, whose talent spanned civil and military affairs and whose conduct was upright, and told him, "Jiaozhi has long lacked a fit governor. I need you to pacify it."

sentences.zh: 祖尚拜謝而出，既而悔之，辭以舊疾。

translations.literal: Zushang bowed in thanks and left, but afterward regretted it and declined on the ground of an old illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zushang thanked him and withdrew, then regretted his acceptance and pleaded an old illness.

sentences.zh: 上遣杜如晦等諭旨曰：「匹夫猶敦然諾，奈何既許朕而復悔之！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Du Ruhui and others to convey his will: "Even a common man keeps his word—how can you, having promised me, turn back!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Du Ruhui and others to say, "Even a common man keeps his word—how can you promise me and then go back on it?"

sentences.zh: 祖尚固辭。

translations.literal: Zushang firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zushang still refused.

sentences.zh: 戊子，上復引見，諭之，祖尚固執不可。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi the emperor summoned him again and urged him; Zushang still obstinately refused.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor received him again and pressed him, but Zushang would not yield.

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「我使人不行，何以為政！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in great anger: "If my orders cannot be carried out, how can I govern!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. "If my orders cannot be obeyed, how can I govern?"

sentences.zh: 命斬於朝堂，尋悔之。

translations.literal: He ordered him beheaded in the court hall and soon regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him executed in the court hall, and soon regretted it.

sentences.zh: 他日，與侍臣論「齊文宣帝何如人？」

translations.literal: Another day, discussing with his attendants, he asked, "What sort of man was Emperor Wenxuan of Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he asked his attendants, "What sort of man was Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi?"

sentences.zh: 魏徵對曰：「文宣狂暴，然人與之爭，事理屈則從之。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng replied: "Wenxuan was violent and fierce, yet when men disputed with him and reason was against him, he yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "Wenxuan was violent, yet when men argued with him and reason was on their side, he yielded.

sentences.zh: 有前青州長史魏愷使於梁還，除光州長史，不肯行，楊遵彥奏之。

translations.literal: There was the former chief secretary of Qingzhou, Wei Kai, who returned from a mission to Liang and was appointed chief secretary of Guangzhou but refused to go; Yang Zunyan memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Kai, former chief secretary of Qingzhou, returned from a mission to Liang and was appointed chief secretary of Guangzhou but refused to go. Yang Zunyan reported him.

sentences.zh: 文宣怒，召而責之。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was angry, summoned him, and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was angry and summoned him to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 愷曰：『臣先任大州，使還，有勞無過，更得小州，此臣所以不行也。』

translations.literal: Kai said: 'Your servant formerly held a large prefecture; on returning from a mission I had merit and no fault, yet I am given a smaller prefecture—that is why your servant will not go.'
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, "I formerly held a large prefecture. After my mission I had merit and no fault, yet I am given a smaller one—that is why I refuse."

sentences.zh: 文宣顧謂遵彥曰：『其言有理，卿赦之。』

translations.literal: Wenxuan turned to Zunyan and said: 'His words have reason—pardon him.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan turned to Zunyan and said, "He speaks with reason. Pardon him."

sentences.zh: 此其所長也。」

translations.literal: That was his strong point."
translations.idiomatic: That was his strength."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "True.

sentences.zh: 向者盧祖尚雖失人臣之義，朕殺之亦為太暴，由此言之，不如文宣矣！」

translations.literal: Lu Zushang just now, though he failed in a minister's duty, for me to kill him was also too violent—by this reckoning I am not the equal of Wenxuan!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zushang failed his duty as a minister, yet for me to kill him was too harsh. By that measure I am not Wenxuan's equal!"

sentences.zh: 命復其官廕。

translations.literal: He ordered Zushang's hereditary privilege restored.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zushang's hereditary privileges restored.

sentences.zh: 徵狀貌不逾中人，而有膽略，善回人主意，每犯顏苦諫；

translations.literal: Zheng's appearance did not surpass an ordinary man, yet he had courage and stratagem, was skilled at turning men's minds, and every time remonstrated to the face with bitter counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was no more than average in looks, yet he was bold and resourceful, skilled at turning the emperor's mind, and remonstrated to his face without flinching;

sentences.zh: 或逢上怒甚，征神色不移，上亦為之霽威。

translations.literal: sometimes when the emperor's anger was extreme, Zheng's expression did not change, and the emperor too would clear his wrath for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: even when the emperor's rage was at its height Zheng's expression never changed, and the emperor would calm himself for him.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁告上塚，還，言於上曰：「人言陛下欲幸南山，外皆嚴裝已畢，而竟不行，何也？」

translations.literal: Once, having asked leave to visit his father's tomb and returned, he said to the emperor: "People say Your Majesty wished to visit the Southern Hills; outside all preparations were complete, yet in the end you did not go—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, after leave to tend his father's tomb, he said to the emperor, "People say you meant to visit the Southern Hills. Outside, everything was ready, yet you did not go—why?"

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「初實有此心，畏卿嗔，故中輟耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "At first I truly had that intent, but I feared your anger and so stopped midway."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed. "I did mean to go, but I feared your displeasure and gave it up halfway."

sentences.zh: 上嘗得佳鷂，自臂之，望見征來，匿懷中；

translations.literal: The emperor once obtained a fine hawk, carried it on his arm himself, and seeing Zheng coming hid it in his bosom;
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had a fine hawk on his arm. Seeing Zheng approach, he hid it in his robe;

sentences.zh: 征奏事固久不已，鷂竟死懷中。

translations.literal: Zheng reported affairs at length without stopping, and the hawk died in his bosom after all.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng went on reporting business at length until the hawk died in his bosom.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛酉，上祀圜丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午，以黃門侍郎王珪為守侍中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renwu, Huangmen Shilang Wang Gui was made acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renwu, Wang Gui, vice minister of the Huangmen, was made acting palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 上嘗閒居，與珪語，有美人侍側，上指示珪曰：「此廬江王瑗之姬也，瑗殺其夫而納之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once at leisure spoke with Gui; a beautiful woman waited at his side. The emperor pointed her out to Gui and said: "This was a concubine of Prince of Lujiang Yuan; Yuan killed her husband and took her in."
translations.idiomatic: Once at leisure the emperor spoke with Gui while a beautiful woman attended him. He pointed to her and said, "This was a concubine of the Prince of Lujiang. Yuan killed her husband and took her."

sentences.zh: 珪避席曰：「陛下以廬江納之為是邪，非邪？」

translations.literal: Gui left his mat and said: "Does Your Majesty consider the Prince of Lujiang's taking her in right, or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose from his mat and asked, "Does Your Majesty think the Prince of Lujiang was right to take her?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「殺人而取其妻，卿何問是非！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He killed a man and took his wife—why do you ask whether it was right or wrong!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He killed a man and took his wife—why ask if that was right or wrong?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔齊桓公知郭公之所以亡，由善善而不能用，然棄其所言之人，管仲以為無異於郭公。

translations.literal: He replied: "Formerly Duke Huan of Qi knew why the lord of Guo perished—because he honored the good yet could not employ them—but he abandoned the man who spoke these words, and Guan Zhong thought him no different from the lord of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Duke Huan of Qi once knew why the lord of Guo fell—he honored the good but could not use them—yet he cast aside the man who told him so. Guan Zhong said he was no better than the lord of Guo.

sentences.zh: 今此美人尚在左右，臣以為聖心是之也。」

translations.literal: Now this beautiful woman is still at Your Majesty's side; your servant thinks the sage heart approves of it."
translations.idiomatic: This woman is still at your side, and I take that to mean Your Majesty approves."

sentences.zh: 上悅，即出之，還其親族。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, immediately released her, and returned her to her kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, released her at once, and sent her back to her family.

sentences.zh: 上使太常少卿祖孝孫教宮人音樂，不稱旨，上責之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zu Xiaosun teach palace women music; it did not please him, and he rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zu Xiaosun, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, teach palace women music. When the result displeased him, he rebuked Zu.

sentences.zh: 溫彥博、王珪諫曰：「孝孫雅士，今乃使之教宮人，又從而譴之，臣竊以為不可。」

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo and Wang Gui remonstrated: "Xiaosun is a refined gentleman; now you have him teach palace women and then reproach him besides—your servants privately think this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo and Wang Gui remonstrated: "Xiaosun is a cultivated gentleman. To set him teaching palace women and then rebuke him besides—we think that wrong."

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「朕置卿等於腹心，當竭忠直以事我，乃附下罔上，為孝孫遊說邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "I placed you at my heart's core; you should exhaust loyalty and forthrightness in serving me—yet you side with inferiors and deceive your superiors, pleading for Xiaosun?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "I placed you at my heart. You should serve me with full loyalty and candor—yet you side with inferiors and deceive your lord, pleading for Xiaosun?"

sentences.zh: 彥博拜謝。

translations.literal: Yanbo bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 珪不拜，曰：「陛下責臣以忠直，今臣所言豈私曲邪！

translations.literal: Gui did not bow and said: "Your Majesty charges your servant with loyalty and forthrightness—are your servant's words now private and crooked!
translations.idiomatic: Gui did not bow. "Your Majesty demands loyalty and candor from me—are my words private and crooked?

sentences.zh: 此乃陛下負臣，非臣負陛下。」

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty failing your servant, not your servant failing Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: It is Your Majesty who has failed me, not I who have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上默然而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 明日，上謂房玄齡曰：「自古帝王納諫誠難，朕昨責溫彥博、王珪、至今悔之。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to Fang Xuanling: "From antiquity it has truly been hard for emperors to accept remonstrance. Yesterday I rebuked Wen Yanbo and Wang Gui and regret it to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told Fang Xuanling, "From antiquity it has been hard for emperors to accept remonstrance. Yesterday I rebuked Wen Yanbo and Wang Gui, and I still regret it.

sentences.zh: 公等勿為此不盡言也。」

translations.literal: Do not, for this reason, fail to speak your full mind."
translations.idiomatic: Do not, for that reason, hold back what you have to say."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為朕養民者，唯在都督、刺史，朕常疏其名於屏風，坐臥觀之，得其在官善惡之跡，皆注於名下，以備黜陟。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Those who nourish the people for me are none but the area commanders and prefects. I often write out their names on a screen and watch them sitting or lying down; whatever I learn of their good or bad conduct in office I note beneath each name to prepare for promotion or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Those who nourish the people for me are the area commanders and prefects. I write their names on a screen and study them day and night. Whatever I learn of their conduct in office I note beneath each name, to guide promotion and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 縣令尤為親民，不可不擇。」

translations.literal: Magistrates are especially close to the people and must not go unchosen."
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates are closest to the people and must be chosen with care."

sentences.zh: 乃命內外五品已上，各舉堪為縣令者，以名聞。

translations.literal: He then ordered all inside and outside the court of fifth rank and above each to recommend men fit to be magistrates and report their names.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every official of fifth rank and above, inside and outside the capital, to recommend men fit to serve as magistrates and report their names.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「比有奴告其主反者，此弊事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Lately there have been slaves who denounced their masters for rebellion—this is a corrupt practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Lately slaves have denounced their masters for treason. That is a corrupt practice.

sentences.zh: 夫謀反不能獨為，必與人共之，何患不發，何必使奴告邪！

translations.literal: Rebellion cannot be plotted alone; one must share it with others—what fear that it will not be exposed? Why must slaves be made to denounce!
translations.idiomatic: Treason cannot be plotted alone; others must be involved. Why fear it will not come to light? Why rely on slaves to accuse their masters?

sentences.zh: 自今有奴告主者，皆勿受，仍斬之。」

translations.literal: From now on, wherever a slave denounces his master, do not accept it; execute the slave instead."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, no denunciation by a slave against his master shall be accepted. Execute the slave instead."

sentences.zh: 西突厥統葉護可汗為其伯父所殺；

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khagan of the Western Turks was killed by his father's elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu, khagan of the Western Turks, was killed by his uncle;

sentences.zh: 伯父自立，是為莫賀咄侯屈利俟毘可汗。

translations.literal: the uncle set himself up and became Khagan Moheduo Houqulisi Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: who set himself up as Khagan Moheduo Houqulisi Pijia.

sentences.zh: 國人不服，弩矢畢部推泥孰莫賀設為可汗，泥孰不可。

translations.literal: The people of the state did not submit; the Nushibi tribe pushed Nishou Moheshe to be khagan, but Nishou would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes would not submit. The Nushibi pushed Nishou Moheshe for the khanship, but Nishou refused.

sentences.zh: 統葉護之子咥力特勒避莫賀咄之禍，亡在康居，泥孰迎而立之，是為乙毘缽羅肆葉護可汗，與莫賀咄相攻，連兵不息，俱遣使來請婚。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu's son Dilitele fled Moheduo's harm and lived in exile in Kangju; Nishou welcomed and set him up as Khagan Yibi Boluo Siyehu. He and Moheduo attacked each other; armies clashed without cease, and both sent envoys to request marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu's son Dilitele fled Moheduo's persecution and took refuge in Kangju. Nishou welcomed him and set him up as Khagan Yibi Boluo Siyehu. He and Moheduo fought without cease, and both sent envoys to request marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 上不許，曰：「汝國方亂，君臣未定，何得言婚！」

translations.literal: The emperor would not consent and said: "Your state is in turmoil; lord and minister are not settled—how can you speak of marriage!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. "Your realm is in turmoil and lord and minister are unsettled—how can you speak of marriage?"

sentences.zh: 且諭以各守部分，勿復相攻。

translations.literal: He also instructed them each to keep to their portions and attack each other no more.
translations.idiomatic: He also told them to keep to their own territories and cease fighting one another.

sentences.zh: 於是西域諸國及敕勒先役屬西突厥者皆叛之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the states of the Western Regions and the Tiele who had formerly been subject to the Western Turks all rebelled against them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the states of the Western Regions and the Tiele tribes formerly subject to the Western Turks all rebelled.

sentences.zh: 突厥北邊諸姓多叛頡利可汗歸薛延陀，共推其俟斤夷男為可汗，夷男不敢當。

translations.literal: Many clans on the northern border of the Turks rebelled against Khagan Jiali and went over to the Xueyantuo; together they pushed their irkin Yinan to be khagan, but Yinan dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Many northern Turkic clans rebelled against Khagan Jiali and joined the Xueyantuo. They wanted to make their irkin Yinan khagan, but Yinan dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 上方圖頡利，遣游擊將軍喬師望間道繼冊書拜夷男為真珠毘伽可汗，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: The emperor was then plotting against Jiali and sent Mobile Cavalry General Qiao Shiwang by a hidden route with a patent of investiture appointing Yinan as Khagan Zhenzhu Pijia, granting drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already planning against Jiali. He sent Mobile Cavalry General Qiao Shiwang by a secret route with a patent appointing Yinan Khagan Zhenzhu Pijia and granting him drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 夷男大喜，遣使入貢，建牙於大漠之郁督軍山下，東至靺鞨，西至西突厥，南接沙磧，北至俱倫水；

translations.literal: Yinan was greatly pleased, sent envoys to offer tribute, and set up his royal camp below Yudujun Mountain in the great desert—east to the Mohe, west to the Western Turks, south touching the sandy wastes, north to the Jülun River;
translations.idiomatic: Yinan was overjoyed, sent tribute envoys, and set up his royal camp below Yudujun Mountain in the great desert—east to the Mohe, west to the Western Turks, south to the sandy wastes, and north to the Jülun River;

sentences.zh: 回紇、拔野古、阿跌、同羅、僕骨、□諸部落皆屬焉。

translations.literal: the Huigu, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and other tribes all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: the Huigu, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and other tribes all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊午，上祀太廟；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day wuwu, the emperor sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuwu the emperor sacrificed at the imperial ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，耕藉於東郊。

translations.literal: on the day guihai he plowed the sacred field at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: on guihai he performed the plowing ceremony at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 沙門法雅坐妖言誅。

translations.literal: The monk Faya was executed for demonic speech.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Faya was executed for sorcerous speech.

sentences.zh: 司空裴寂嘗聞其言，辛未，寂坐免官，遣還鄉里。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Pei Ji had once heard his words; on the day xinwei Ji was removed from office on that account and sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Pei Ji had once heard him speak. On xinwei Ji was dismissed from office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 寂請留京師，上數之曰：「計公勳庸，安得至此！

translations.literal: Ji asked to remain in the capital. The emperor rebuked him: "Considering your merit and service, how did you reach this rank!
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked to remain in the capital. The emperor rebuked him: "By your merit alone, how did you ever rise so high?

sentences.zh: 直以恩澤為群臣第一。

translations.literal: It was solely through favor that you stood first among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: You stand first among the ministers only through my favor.

sentences.zh: 武德之際貨賂公行，紀綱紊亂，皆公之由也，但以故舊不忍盡法。

translations.literal: In the Wude era bribes were openly exchanged and discipline was in disorder—all through you. Only because you are an old associate have I not applied the full penalty of law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude, bribery ran rampant and discipline collapsed—all through you. Only because you are an old friend have I not punished you to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 得歸守墳墓，幸已多矣！」

translations.literal: To be able to return and guard your ancestral graves—you are already more fortunate than you deserve!"
translations.idiomatic: To go home and tend your ancestors' graves is more fortune than you deserve!"

sentences.zh: 寂遂歸蒲州。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon returned to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then returned to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又坐狂人信行言寂有天命，寂不以聞，當死；

translations.literal: Before long he was again implicated because the madman Xinxing said Ji had the Mandate of Heaven and Ji did not report it—he deserved death;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was implicated again when the madman Xinxing said Ji had Heaven's mandate and Ji failed to report it. He deserved death;

sentences.zh: 流靜州。

translations.literal: he was banished to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: he was banished to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會山羌作亂，或言劫寂為主。

translations.literal: When the Shan Qiang rebelled, some said they would seize Ji and make him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shan Qiang rebelled, some said the rebels would seize Ji and make him their leader.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「寂當死，我生之，必不然也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ji ought to have died; I spared his life—it will certainly not be so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ji should have died, yet I spared him. That will certainly not happen."

sentences.zh: 俄聞寂帥家僮破賊。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Ji had led his household retainers and defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came word that Ji had led his household retainers and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 上思其佐命之功，征入朝，會卒。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled his merit in founding the dynasty and summoned him to court, but Ji died on the way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of Ji's service in founding the dynasty, summoned him to court, but Ji died en route.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊寅，以房玄齡為左僕射，杜如晦為右僕射，以尚書右丞魏徵守秘書監，參預朝政。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day wuyin, Fang Xuanling was made Left Vice Director, Du Ruhui Right Vice Director, and Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng was appointed acting Secretariat Director to participate in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuyin, Fang Xuanling was appointed Left Vice Director and Du Ruhui Right Vice Director; Wei Zheng, Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat, was named acting Secretariat Director and admitted to deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月，己酉，上錄系囚。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiyou, the emperor reviewed prisoners in custody.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiyou, the emperor reviewed prisoners held in custody.

sentences.zh: 有劉恭者，頸有「勝」文，自云「當勝天下」，坐是繫獄。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Gong, who had the character sheng on his neck and declared that he would conquer all under Heaven; for this he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: One prisoner, Liu Gong, bore the character sheng on his neck and claimed he was destined to conquer the realm; for this he had been jailed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「若天將興之，非朕所能除；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If Heaven is about to raise him up, it is not within my power to remove him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If Heaven intends to raise him up, I cannot remove him;

sentences.zh: 若無天命，『勝』文何為！」

translations.literal: if there is no mandate of Heaven, what is the point of the character sheng!"
translations.idiomatic: if there is no mandate of Heaven, what use is the character sheng!

sentences.zh: 乃釋之。

translations.literal: He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He then released him.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上謂房玄齡、杜如晦曰：「公為僕射，當廣求賢人，隨才授任，此宰相之職也。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi the emperor said to Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui: "As Vice Directors you should widely seek out men of talent and assign posts according to their abilities—this is the duty of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor told Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, "As Vice Directors you should seek talent broadly and appoint men according to their abilities. That is a chief minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 比聞聽受辭訟，日不暇給，安能助朕求賢乎！」

translations.literal: Lately I hear you hear lawsuits, with not a day to spare—how can you help me seek talent!"
translations.idiomatic: Lately I hear you spend your days hearing lawsuits, with no time to spare—how can you help me find talent!

sentences.zh: 因敕「尚書細務屬左右丞，唯大事應奏者，乃關僕射。」

translations.literal: He therefore ordered: "Detailed affairs of the Secretariat belong to the left and right assistants; only major matters requiring memorial should be referred to the Vice Directors."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered that detailed Secretariat business should fall to the left and right assistants, and only major matters requiring memorial should be brought to the Vice Directors."

sentences.zh: 玄齡明達吏事，輔以文學，夙夜盡心，惟恐一物失所；

translations.literal: Xuanling was clear and adept in administrative affairs, aided by literary learning; day and night he gave his full heart, fearing only that one thing might go astray;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling was clear and adept in administrative affairs and well versed in letters; day and night he gave himself wholly to duty, fearing only that something might go wrong;

sentences.zh: 用法寬平，聞人有善，若己有之，不以求備取人，不以己長格物。

translations.literal: in applying the law he was lenient and even-handed; when he heard of another's good quality he rejoiced as if it were his own; he did not demand perfection in choosing men, nor measure others by his own strengths.
translations.idiomatic: he applied the law with leniency and fairness; when he heard of another's virtue he rejoiced as though it were his own; he did not demand perfection in men, nor judge others by his own strengths.

sentences.zh: 與杜如晦引拔士類，常如不及。

translations.literal: With Du Ruhui he promoted men of the scholar class, always as though he could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Ruhui he promoted scholars, always as though he could never do enough.

sentences.zh: 至於台閣規模，皆二人所定。

translations.literal: As for the structure of the central administration, it was all set by these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The structure of the central administration was entirely their work.

sentences.zh: 上每與玄齡謀事，必曰：「非如晦不能決。」

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor deliberated with Xuanling on affairs, he would always say: "Without Ruhui this cannot be decided."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor deliberated with Xuanling, he would say, "This cannot be decided without Ruhui.

sentences.zh: 及如晦至，卒用玄齡之策。

translations.literal: When Ruhui arrived, in the end Xuanling's plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruhui arrived, Xuanling's plan was always the one adopted.

sentences.zh: 蓋玄齡善謀，如晦能斷故也。

translations.literal: This was because Xuanling was good at planning and Ruhui was able to decide.
translations.idiomatic: For Xuanling excelled at planning and Ruhui at deciding.

sentences.zh: 二人深相得，同心徇國，故唐世稱賢相者，推房、杜焉。

translations.literal: The two were deeply attuned to each other and of one mind in serving the state; hence among those called worthy chief ministers in Tang times, Fang and Du are foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply attuned and of one mind in serving the state, they were held up in Tang times as the model of worthy chief ministers—Fang and Du.

sentences.zh: 玄齡雖蒙寵待，或以事被譴，輒累日詣朝堂，稽顙請罪，恐懼若無所容。

translations.literal: Although Xuanling enjoyed favor, when rebuked over some matter he would for days on end come to the court hall, bow with forehead to the ground and beg forgiveness, in fear as though he had no place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Though favored, when rebuked over some matter Xuanling would for days come to the court hall, prostrate himself, and beg forgiveness, trembling as though he had nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 玄齡監修國史，上語之曰：「比見《漢書》載《子虛》、《上林賦》，浮華無用。

translations.literal: Xuanling supervised the compilation of the national history. The emperor said to him: "Lately I have seen the Book of Han record the 'Rhapsody of Sir Fantasy' and the 'Rhapsody of the Upper Forest'—ornate and useless.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanling supervised compilation of the national history, the emperor told him, "I have lately seen the Book of Han include the Rhapsody of Sir Fantasy and the Rhapsody of the Upper Forest—ornate and useless.

sentences.zh: 其上書論事，詞理切直者，朕從與不從，皆當載之。」

translations.literal: When ministers submit memorials discussing affairs, those whose language and reasoning are direct and forthright—whether I follow them or not—should all be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: When ministers submit memorials on affairs of state, those whose words are direct and reasoned—whether I follow their advice or not—should all be recorded."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，上皇徙居弘義宮，更名大安宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yihai, the retired emperor moved to Hongyi Palace, which was renamed Dayan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, the retired emperor moved to Hongyi Palace, renamed Dayan Palace.

sentences.zh: 上始御太極殿，謂侍臣曰：「中書、門下，機要之司，詔敕有不便者，皆應論執。

translations.literal: The emperor began holding court in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and said to his attending ministers: "The Secretariat and Chancellery are offices of vital importance; when edicts and orders are unsuitable, all should debate and hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began holding court in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and told his ministers, "The Secretariat and Chancellery are offices of vital importance. When an edict is unsuitable, you should debate and hold firm.

sentences.zh: 比來唯睹順從，不聞違異。

translations.literal: Lately I have seen only compliance and heard no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have seen only compliance and heard no dissent.

sentences.zh: 若但行文書，則誰不可為，何必擇才也！」

translations.literal: If you merely transmit documents, then who cannot do it—why must talent be chosen!"
translations.idiomatic: If you merely transmit documents, anyone could do the job—why choose men of talent at all!

sentences.zh: 房玄齡等皆頓首謝。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and the others all bowed with foreheads to the ground in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and the others all prostrated themselves in apology.

sentences.zh: 故事：凡軍國大事，則中書舍人各執所見，雜署其名，謂之五花判事。

translations.literal: By precedent: for all major military and state affairs, the Secretariat drafters each held to their own view and signed their names together, which was called the five-flower memorial system.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, on major military and state affairs each Secretariat drafter recorded his own view and all signed together—the five-flower memorial system.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、中書令省審之，給事中、黃門侍郎駁正之。

translations.literal: The Vice Director and Director of the Secretariat examined them; the Supervising Secretary and Vice Director of the Chancellery corrected and revised them.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director and Director of the Secretariat reviewed them; the Supervising Secretary and Vice Director of the Chancellery corrected and revised them.

sentences.zh: 上始申明舊制，由是鮮有敗事。

translations.literal: The emperor now clarified the old system, and from this there were few failures in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now clarified the old system, and from then on few matters went wrong.

sentences.zh: 茌平人馬周，客遊長安，捨於中郎將常何之家。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou of Chiping, traveling as a guest in Chang'an, lodged at the home of General of the Palace Gentlemen Chang He.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou of Chiping, a guest in Chang'an, lodged with General of the Palace Gentlemen Chang He.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬午，以旱，詔文武官極言得失。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renwu, because of drought an edict ordered civil and military officials to speak freely of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renwu, drought prompted an edict calling on civil and military officials to speak freely of what was going wrong.

sentences.zh: 何武人不學，不知所言，周代之陳便宜二十餘條。

translations.literal: He was a military man without learning and did not know what to say; Zhou drafted more than twenty items of practical advice on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chang He, a military man without learning, did not know what to say; Zhou drafted more than twenty practical recommendations for him.

sentences.zh: 上怪其能，以問何，對曰：「此非臣所能，家客馬周為臣具草耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his ability and questioned He, who replied: "This is not within your servant's power; my house guest Ma Zhou drafted it for your servant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at the quality and questioned Chang He, who replied, "This is not my work; my house guest Ma Zhou drafted it for me.

sentences.zh: 上即召之；

translations.literal: The emperor at once summoned him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once summoned Zhou;

sentences.zh: 未至，遣使督促者數輩。

translations.literal: before he arrived, several envoys were sent in succession to hurry him.
translations.idiomatic: and before Zhou arrived sent several envoys in succession to hurry him along.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，與語，甚悅，令直門下省，尋除監察御史，奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience and the emperor spoke with him, he was greatly pleased; Zhou was ordered to serve at the Chancellery, and soon was appointed Investigating Censor; on missions he fully answered the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou was received in audience the emperor was greatly pleased; he was assigned to the Chancellery and soon made Investigating Censor, and on missions carried out the emperor's intent admirably.

sentences.zh: 上以常何為知人，賜絹三百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Chang He a man who knew talent and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Chang He a man who knew talent and rewarded him with three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，己巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day jisi, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the first day jisi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丙子，薛延陀毘伽可汗遣其弟統特勒入貢，上賜以寶刀及寶鞭，謂曰：「卿所部有大罪者斬之，小罪者鞭之。」

translations.literal: On the day bingzi the Xueyantuo khan Piluo sent his younger brother Tongte'er to pay tribute; the emperor bestowed a precious sword and a precious whip and said: "Among your following, those guilty of great crimes execute; those guilty of lesser crimes whip."
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Xueyantuo khan Piluo sent his younger brother Tongte'er to pay tribute. The emperor gave him a precious sword and whip and said, "Among your followers, execute those guilty of great crimes and whip those guilty of lesser ones.

sentences.zh: 夷男甚喜。

translations.literal: Yinan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗大懼，始遣使稱臣，請尚公主，修婿禮。

translations.literal: The Eastern Turk khagan Jiali was greatly afraid and for the first time sent envoys declaring himself a subject, requesting marriage to a princess and observing the rites of a son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Turk khagan Jiali was greatly afraid and for the first time sent envoys declaring himself a subject, requesting a princess in marriage and the rites due a son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 代州都督張公謹上言突厥可取之狀，以為：「頡利縱欲逞暴，誅忠良，暱奸佞，一也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongjin, military governor of Daizhou, submitted a memorial on the conditions under which the Turks could be taken, arguing: "Jiali indulges his desires and acts with violence, executes the loyal and good, and favors the wicked and sycophantic—first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongjin, military governor of Daizhou, submitted a memorial on how the Turks could be taken, arguing: "First, Jiali indulges his desires and acts with violence, executes the loyal, and favors the wicked and sycophantic.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀等諸部皆叛，二也。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo and other tribes have all rebelled—second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Xueyantuo and other tribes have all rebelled.

sentences.zh: 突利、拓設、欲谷設皆得罪，無所自容，三也。

translations.literal: Tuli, Tuoshe, and Yugushe have all been found guilty and have nowhere to turn—third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Tuli, Tuoshe, and Yugushe have all fallen afoul of him and have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 塞北霜早，餱糧乏絕，四也。

translations.literal: North of the passes frost came early and provisions are exhausted—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, north of the passes frost came early and provisions are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 頡利疏其族類，親委諸胡，胡人反覆，大軍一臨，必生內變，五也，華人入北，其眾甚多，比聞所在嘯聚，保據山險，大軍出塞，自然響應，六也。」

translations.literal: Jiali has estranged his own clansmen and entrusted affairs to various Hu; the Hu are fickle—when a great army arrives, internal revolt is sure to arise—fifth. Chinese who have gone north are very numerous; lately I hear they are gathering everywhere, holding mountain strongholds; when a great army crosses the frontier, they will naturally respond—sixth."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Jiali has estranged his own clansmen and entrusted power to various Hu peoples, who are fickle—when a great army arrives, internal revolt is sure to follow. Sixth, many Chinese have gone north; lately I hear they are gathering everywhere and holding mountain strongholds—when a great army crosses the frontier, they will naturally rise in response.

sentences.zh: 上以頡利可汗既請和親，復援梁師都，丁亥，命兵部尚書李靖為行軍總管討之，以張公謹為副。

translations.literal: Although the khagan Jiali had requested marriage alliance, he again supported Liang Shidu; on the day dinghai the emperor appointed Li Jing, Minister of War, commander of the campaign army to attack him, with Zhang Gongjin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jiali had requested a marriage alliance, he again supported Liang Shidu; on dinghai the emperor appointed Minister of War Li Jing commander of the campaign army to attack him, with Zhang Gongjin as deputy.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，突厥俟斤九人帥三千騎來降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingwu, nine Turkic irkins leading three thousand horsemen came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, nine Turkic irkins leading three thousand horsemen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 戊午，拔野古、僕骨、同羅、奚酋長並帥眾來降。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu the chiefs of Bayegu, Pugu, Tongluo, and Xi all led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the chiefs of Bayegu, Pugu, Tongluo, and Xi all led their followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛丑，突厥寇河西，肅州刺史公孫武達、甘州刺史成仁重與戰，破之，捕虜千餘口。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day xinchou, the Turks raided Hexi; Gongsun Wuda, prefect of Suzhou, and Cheng Renzhong, prefect of Ganzhou, fought them, defeated them, and captured more than a thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinchou, Turks raided Hexi; Gongsun Wuda, prefect of Suzhou, and Cheng Renzhong, prefect of Ganzhou, defeated them and took more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 上遣使至涼州，都督李大亮有佳鷹，使者諷大亮使獻之，大亮密表曰：「陛下久絕畋游而使者求鷹。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to Liangzhou; Military Governor Li Daliang had an excellent hawk, and the envoy hinted that Daliang should present it. Daliang submitted a secret memorial saying: "Your Majesty long ago gave up hunting, yet the envoy seeks a hawk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to Liangzhou. Military Governor Li Daliang had an excellent hawk, and the envoy hinted that Daliang should present it. Daliang submitted a secret memorial: "Your Majesty long ago gave up hunting, yet the envoy seeks a hawk.

sentences.zh: 若陛下之意，深乖昔旨；

translations.literal: If this is Your Majesty's intent, it deeply departs from your former purpose;
translations.idiomatic: If this is Your Majesty's intent, it deeply departs from your former purpose;

sentences.zh: 如其自擅，乃是使非其人。」

translations.literal: if he acted on his own, then the wrong man was sent as envoy."
translations.idiomatic: if he acted on his own, then the wrong man was sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上謂侍臣曰：「李大亮可謂忠直。」

translations.literal: On the day guimao the emperor said to his attending ministers: "Li Daliang may be called loyal and forthright."
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor told his ministers, "Li Daliang may truly be called loyal and forthright.

sentences.zh: 手詔褒美，賜以胡瓶及荀悅《漢紀》。

translations.literal: By his own hand he issued an edict praising him and bestowed a foreign vase and Xun Yue's Annals of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a personal edict praising him and bestowed a foreign vase and Xun Yue's Annals of Han.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以并州都督李世勣為通漢道行軍總管，兵部尚書李靖為定襄道行軍總管，華州刺史柴紹為金河道行軍總管，靈州大都督薛萬徹為暢武道行軍總管，眾合十餘萬，皆受李靖節度，分道出擊突厥。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen Li Shiji, military governor of Bingzhou, was made commander of the Tonghan Route campaign army; Li Jing, Minister of War, commander of the Dingxiang Route campaign army; Chai Shao, prefect of Huazhou, commander of the Jinhe Route campaign army; and Xue Wanche, grand defender of Lingzhou, commander of the Changwu Route campaign army. Their forces totaled more than one hundred thousand, all under Li Jing's command, advancing by separate routes to strike the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Li Shiji, military governor of Bingzhou, was made commander of the Tonghan Route army; Minister of War Li Jing commander of the Dingxiang Route army; Chai Shao, prefect of Huazhou, commander of the Jinhe Route army; and Xue Wanche, grand defender of Lingzhou, commander of the Changwu Route army. More than one hundred thousand troops, all under Li Jing's command, advanced by separate routes against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，任城王道宗擊突厥於靈州，破之。

translations.literal: On the day yichou Prince Daozong of Rencheng attacked the Turks at Lingzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Prince Daozong of Rencheng attacked the Turks at Lingzhou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊辰，突利可汗入朝，上謂侍臣曰：「往者太上皇以百姓之故，稱臣於突厥，朕常痛心。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wuchen, the khagan Tuli came to court. The emperor said to his attending ministers: "In the past the retired emperor, for the sake of the people, declared himself subject to the Turks—I have always grieved at this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuchen, the khagan Tuli came to court. The emperor told his ministers, "In the past the retired emperor, for the people's sake, declared himself subject to the Turks—I have always grieved at this.

sentences.zh: 今單于稽顙，庶幾可雪前恥。」

translations.literal: Now the chanyu bows with forehead to the ground—perhaps the former shame can be wiped away."
translations.idiomatic: Now the chanyu bows with his forehead to the ground—perhaps the old shame can at last be wiped away."

sentences.zh: 壬午，靺鞨遣使入貢，上曰：「靺鞨遠來，蓋突厥已服之故也。

translations.literal: On the day renwu the Mohe sent envoys to pay tribute. The emperor said: "The Mohe have come from afar—surely because the Turks have already submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Mohe sent envoys to pay tribute. The emperor said, "The Mohe have come from afar—surely because the Turks have already submitted.

sentences.zh: 昔人謂御戎無上策，朕今治安中國，而四夷自服，豈非上策乎！」

translations.literal: Men of old said there was no best policy for controlling the barbarians; I now keep peace within China, and the four quarters submit of themselves—is this not the best policy!"
translations.idiomatic: Men of old said there was no best policy for controlling the barbarians; I now keep peace within China, and the four quarters submit of themselves—is this not the best policy!"

sentences.zh: 癸未，右僕射杜如晦以疾遜位，上許之。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei Right Vice Director Du Ruhui resigned his post because of illness, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Right Vice Director Du Ruhui resigned because of illness, and the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上問給事中孔穎達曰：「《論語》：『以能問於不能，以多問於寡，有若無，實若虛。』

translations.literal: On the day yiyou the emperor asked Supervising Secretary Kong Yingda: "In the Analects: 'The able ask the unable; the many ask the few; having as though not having; full as though empty.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the emperor asked Supervising Secretary Kong Yingda, "In the Analects: 'The able ask the unable; the many ask the few; having as though not having; full as though empty.

sentences.zh: 何謂也？」

translations.literal: What does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: What does this mean?'

sentences.zh: 穎達具釋其義以對，且曰：「非獨匹夫如是，帝王亦然。

translations.literal: Yingda fully explained its meaning in reply and said: "It is not only common men who should be so—emperors likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda fully explained its meaning and added, "It is not only common men who should be so—emperors likewise.

sentences.zh: 帝王內蘊神明，外當玄默，故《易》稱『以蒙養正，以明夷蒞眾。』

translations.literal: Emperors harbor divine insight within and outwardly should be darkly silent; hence the Changes says, 'Nourish the upright through obscurity; approach the multitude through Brightness Hidden.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperors harbor divine insight within and outwardly should be darkly silent; hence the Changes says, 'Nourish the upright through obscurity; approach the multitude through Brightness Hidden.

sentences.zh: 若位居尊極，炫耀聰明，以才陵人，飾非拒諫，則下情不通，取亡之道也。」

translations.literal: If one occupies the highest rank yet displays one's brilliance, overwhelms others with talent, covers faults and rejects remonstrance, then the feelings of those below cannot reach upward—this is the way to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: If one occupies the highest rank yet displays one's brilliance, overwhelms others with talent, covers faults and rejects remonstrance, then the feelings of those below cannot reach upward—this is the way to ruin.

sentences.zh: 上深善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply approved his words.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，突厥郁射設帥所部來降。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin the Turk Yugushe led his following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the Turk Yugushe led his following to surrender.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁未，東謝酋長謝元深、南謝酋長謝強來朝。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day dingwei, the Eastern Xie chief Xie Yuanshen and the Southern Xie chief Xie Qiang came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingwei, the Eastern Xie chief Xie Yuanshen and the Southern Xie chief Xie Qiang came to court.

sentences.zh: 諸謝皆南蠻別種，在黔州之西。

translations.literal: The various Xie were separate branches of the southern Man, west of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The various Xie were separate branches of the southern Man peoples, west of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以東謝為應州、南謝為莊州，隸黔州都督。

translations.literal: An edict made the Eastern Xie into Yingzhou and the Southern Xie into Zhuangzhou, both subordinate to the military governor of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made the Eastern Xie into Yingzhou and the Southern Xie into Zhuangzhou, both under the military governor of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時遠方諸國來朝貢者甚眾，服裝詭異，中書侍郎顏師古請圖寫以示後，作《王會圖》，從之。

translations.literal: At this time many distant states came to court with tribute; their dress was strange and varied. Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu requested that they be painted to show posterity, and compiled the Wang Hui Tu; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time many distant states came to court with tribute, their dress strange and varied. Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu asked that they be painted for posterity and compiled the Wang Hui Tu; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，牂柯酋長謝能羽及充州蠻入貢，詔以牂柯為牂州；

translations.literal: On the day yichou the Zangke chief Xie Nengyu and the Man of Chongzhou paid tribute; an edict made Zangke into Zangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Zangke chief Xie Nengyu and the Man of Chongzhou paid tribute; an edict made Zangke into Zangzhou;

sentences.zh: 黨頃酋長細封步賴來降，以其地為軌州；

translations.literal: the Tangut chief Xifeng Bulai came to surrender, and his territory was made into Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: the Tangut chief Xifeng Bulai surrendered, and his territory was made into Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 各以其酋長為刺史。

translations.literal: in each case the chief was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: in each case the chief was made prefect.

sentences.zh: 党項地亙三千里，姓別為部，不相統壹，細封氏、費聽氏、往利氏、頗超氏、野辭氏、旁當氏、米擒氏、拓跋氏，皆大姓也。

translations.literal: Tangut lands stretched three thousand li; surnames divided them into tribes without unified rule—the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Pangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans were all great lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut lands stretched three thousand li; divided by surname into tribes without unified rule—the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Pangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans were all great lineages.

sentences.zh: 步賴既為唐所禮，餘部相繼來降，以其地為崌、奉、巖、遠四州。

translations.literal: Once Bulai had been honored by Tang, the remaining tribes came to surrender in succession, and their lands were made into the four prefectures of Ji, Feng, Yan, and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bulai had been honored by Tang, the remaining tribes surrendered in succession, and their lands were made into the four prefectures of Ji, Feng, Yan, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部奏：中國人自塞外歸，及四夷前後降附者，男子一百二十餘萬口。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported: Chinese returning from beyond the frontier, together with men of the four quarters who had submitted before and after, totaled more than 1.2 million males.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue reported that Chinese returning from beyond the frontier, together with men of the four quarters who had submitted before and after, totaled more than 1.2 million males.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡、珪掌內外官考，治書侍御史萬年權萬紀奏其不平，上命侯君集推之。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Gui conducted the evaluation of inner and outer officials; Investigating Censor of Wannian Quan Wanji memorialized that it was unfair, and the emperor ordered Hou Junji to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Wang Gui conducted the evaluation of inner and outer officials; Investigating Censor Quan Wanji of Wannian memorialized that it was unfair, and the emperor ordered Hou Junji to investigate.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「玄齡、珪皆朝廷舊臣，素以忠直為陛下所委，所考既多，其間能無一二人不當！

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Xuanling and Gui are both old ministers of the court, long entrusted by Your Majesty for loyalty and forthrightness; the men evaluated were many—among them can there fail to be one or two who were wrongly rated!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated, "Xuanling and Gui are both old ministers of the court, long entrusted by Your Majesty for their loyalty and forthrightness. They evaluated many men—among so many, can there fail to be one or two wrongly rated!

sentences.zh: 察其情，終非阿私。

translations.literal: Examining their intent, in the end it was not partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Examining their intent, it was not partiality.

sentences.zh: 若推得其事，則皆不可信，豈得復當重任！

translations.literal: If investigation proves the charge, then neither can be trusted—how can they again bear heavy responsibility!
translations.idiomatic: If investigation proves the charge, then neither can be trusted—how can they again bear heavy responsibility!

sentences.zh: 且萬紀比來恆在考堂，曾無駁正；

translations.literal: Moreover Wanji has constantly been in the evaluation hall lately and never once raised an objection;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wanji has constantly been in the evaluation hall and never once raised an objection;

sentences.zh: 及身不得考，乃始陳論。

translations.literal: only when he himself was not rated well did he begin to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: only when he himself was rated poorly did he begin to speak out.

sentences.zh: 此正欲激陛下之怒，非竭誠徇國也。

translations.literal: This is precisely an attempt to stir Your Majesty's anger—not wholehearted service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely an attempt to stir Your Majesty's anger—not wholehearted service to the state.

sentences.zh: 使推之得實，未足裨益朝廷；

translations.literal: Even if investigation proves the facts, it will not benefit the court;
translations.idiomatic: Even if investigation proves the facts, it will not benefit the court;

sentences.zh: 若其本虛，徒失陛下委任大臣之意。

translations.literal: if the charge is baseless, it will only waste Your Majesty's intent in entrusting chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: if the charge is baseless, it will only undermine Your Majesty's trust in his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 臣所愛者治體，非敢苟私二臣。」

translations.literal: What your servant cares for is the health of governance—not daring to favor the two ministers privately."
translations.idiomatic: What I care for is the health of governance—I do not dare favor the two ministers privately.

sentences.zh: 上乃釋不問。

translations.literal: The emperor then released the matter and pursued it no further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 濮州刺史龐相壽坐貪污解任，自陳嘗在秦王幕府；

translations.literal: Pang Xiangshou, prefect of Puzhou, was removed from office for corruption and declared that he had once served on the Prince of Qin's staff;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xiangshou, prefect of Puzhou, was removed from office for corruption and pleaded that he had once served on the Prince of Qin's staff;

sentences.zh: 上憐之，欲聽還舊任。

translations.literal: the emperor took pity on him and wished to allow him to return to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and wished to restore him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「秦府左右，中外甚多，恐人人皆恃恩私，是使為善者懼。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Those who served on the Prince of Qin's staff, inside and outside the court, are very many—I fear each will rely on private favor, which will make those who do good afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated, "Those who served on the Prince of Qin's staff, inside and outside the court, are very many—I fear each will rely on private favor, which will make those who do good afraid.

sentences.zh: 上欣然納之，謂相壽曰：「我昔為秦王，乃一府之主；

translations.literal: The emperor gladly accepted this and said to Xiangshou: "When I was Prince of Qin, I was master of one household;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly accepted and told Xiangshou, "When I was Prince of Qin, I was master of one household;

sentences.zh: 今居大位，乃四海之主，不得獨私故人。

translations.literal: now I occupy the great throne and am master of all under Heaven—I cannot favor old associates alone.
translations.idiomatic: now I occupy the throne and am master of all under Heaven—I cannot favor old associates alone.

sentences.zh: 大臣所執如是，朕何敢違！」

translations.literal: When my ministers hold to such a view, how dare I disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: When my ministers hold so firm to principle, how dare I go against them!

sentences.zh: 賜帛遣之。

translations.literal: He granted him silk and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Xiangshou silk as a gift and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 相壽流涕而去。

translations.literal: Xiangshou wept as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshou left in tears.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，李靖帥驍騎三千自馬邑進屯惡陽嶺，夜襲定襄，破之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Li Jing led three thousand elite cavalry from Mayi, advanced and encamped at Eyang Ridge, and by night attacked Dingxiang, defeating it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Li Jing led three thousand elite cavalry from Mayi, advanced to Eyang Ridge, and launched a night attack on Dingxiang, breaking the enemy.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗不意靖猝至，大驚曰：「唐不傾國而來，靖何敢孤軍至此！」

translations.literal: Jiali Qaghan of the Turks did not expect Jing to arrive so suddenly. Greatly startled, he said: "If Tang did not come with the whole nation, how dare Jing come here with a lone army!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiali Qaghan of the Turks had not expected Jing to appear so suddenly. He was greatly alarmed and exclaimed, "Would Tang send its entire strength? How dare Jing come this far with a lone army!

sentences.zh: 其從一日數驚，乃徙牙於磧口。

translations.literal: His followers were alarmed several times in a single day, whereupon he moved his court to Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: His followers grew alarmed again and again within a single day, and he moved his royal camp to Qikou.

sentences.zh: 靖復遣諜離其心腹，頡利所親康蘇密以隋蕭后及煬帝之孫政道來降。

translations.literal: Jing again sent spies to sow dissension among Jiali's close followers. Kang Sumi, whom Jiali trusted, came over to Tang with Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao, grandson of Emperor Yang of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent spies once more to turn Jiali's inner circle against him. Kang Sumi, a man Jiali held dear, defected with Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao, the grandson of Emperor Yang of Sui.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至京師。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, they arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，有降胡言「中國人或潛通書啟於蕭後者」。

translations.literal: Earlier, a surrendered Turk had said, "Some people of China may secretly send letters to Empress Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a surrendered Turk had reported that some Chinese had secretly exchanged letters with Empress Xiao.

sentences.zh: 至是，中書舍人楊文瓘請鞫之，上曰：「天下未定，突厥方強，愚民無知，或有斯事。

translations.literal: At this point Zhongshu Sheren Yang Wenguan requested to investigate it. The emperor said: "The realm was not yet settled and the Turks were still strong; ignorant common people, knowing nothing, may have done such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhongshu Sheren Yang Wenguan asked to investigate. The emperor said, "When the realm was still unsettled and the Turks still strong, ignorant folk might well have done such a thing.

sentences.zh: 今天下已安，既往之罪，何須問也！」

translations.literal: Now the realm is already at peace—why need one inquire into past offenses!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is secure; what need is there to dredge up old offenses!"

sentences.zh: 李世勣出雲中，與突厥戰於白道，大破之。

translations.literal: Li Shiji marched out from Yunzhong, fought the Turks at Baidao, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji marched out from Yunzhong, fought the Turks at Baidao, and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，上幸驪山溫湯。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jihai, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，李靖破突厥頡利可汗於陰山。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Li Jing defeated Jiali Qaghan of the Turks at Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Li Jing defeated Jiali Qaghan of the Turks at Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，頡利既敗，竄於鐵山，餘眾尚數萬；

translations.literal: Earlier, after Jiali had been defeated, he fled to Tieshan; his remaining forces still numbered in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after his defeat, Jiali had fled to Tieshan, and his remaining forces still numbered in the tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 遣執失思力入見，謝罪，請舉國內附，身自入朝。

translations.literal: he sent Zhisi-li to enter court, confess his offenses, request that the whole nation submit, and come personally to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Zhisi-li to court to confess his offenses, offer the submission of the whole nation, and pledge to come in person to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 上遣鴻臚卿唐儉等慰撫之，又詔李靖將兵迎頡利。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and others to comfort and reassure him, and also ordered Li Jing to lead troops to receive Jiali.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and others to comfort and reassure him, and also ordered Li Jing to lead troops to escort Jiali in.

sentences.zh: 頡利外為卑辭，內實猶豫，欲俟草青馬肥，亡入漠北。

translations.literal: Outwardly Jiali spoke humbly, but inwardly he hesitated, intending to wait until the grass turned green and the horses grew fat, then flee north into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Jiali spoke humbly, but inwardly he hesitated, planning to wait until the grass turned green and the horses grew fat, then flee north into the desert.

sentences.zh: 靖引兵與李世勣會白道，相與謀曰：「頡利雖敗，其眾猶盛，若走度磧北，保依九姓，道阻且遠，追之難及。

translations.literal: Jing led his troops to join Li Shiji at Baidao, and together they plotted: "Though Jiali is defeated, his forces are still numerous. If he flees across the northern desert and takes refuge with the Nine Surnamed tribes, the route will be difficult and distant and pursuit hard to overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led his troops to join Li Shiji at Baidao, and together they plotted: "Though Jiali is defeated, his forces are still numerous. If he flees across the northern desert and takes refuge with the Nine Surnamed tribes, the route will be difficult and distant, and pursuit will be hard to overtake.

sentences.zh: 今詔使至彼，虜必自寬，若選精騎一萬，繼二十日糧往襲之，不戰可擒矣。」

translations.literal: Now that the imperial envoy has reached him, the barbarians will surely relax their guard. If we select ten thousand elite cavalry, carry twenty days' provisions, and raid them, we can capture them without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial envoy has reached him, the barbarians will surely relax their guard. If we select ten thousand elite cavalry, carry twenty days' provisions, and strike them, we can capture them without a battle."

sentences.zh: 以其謀告張公謹，公謹曰：「詔書已許其降，使者在彼，奈何擊之！」

translations.literal: He told his plan to Zhang Gongjin. Gongjin said: "The imperial edict has already granted their surrender, and the envoy is there—how can we attack them!"
translations.idiomatic: He told his plan to Zhang Gongjin. Gongjin said, "The imperial edict has already granted their surrender, and the envoy is there—how can we attack them!

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「此韓信所以破齊也。

translations.literal: Jing said: "This is how Han Xin broke Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "This is how Han Xin broke Qi.

sentences.zh: 唐儉輩何足惜！」

translations.literal: What are men like Tang Jian worth regretting!"
translations.idiomatic: What are men like Tang Jian worth regretting!

sentences.zh: 遂勒兵夜發，世勣繼之，軍至陰山，遇突厥千餘帳，俘以隨軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the army to march out by night; Shiji followed. When the army reached Yinshan, they encountered more than a thousand Turk yurts and took the people captive to accompany the army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered the army to march out by night; Shiji followed. When the army reached Yinshan, they encountered more than a thousand Turk yurts and took the inhabitants captive to accompany the column.

sentences.zh: 頡利見使者，大喜，意自安。

translations.literal: Jiali saw the envoy and was greatly pleased; his mind grew easy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiali saw the envoy, he was greatly pleased and his mind grew easy.

sentences.zh: 靖使武邑蘇定方帥二百騎為前鋒，乘霧而行，去牙帳七里，虜乃覺之。

translations.literal: Jing had Su Dingfang of Wuyi lead two hundred cavalry as vanguard; riding through the fog, when still seven li from the royal camp, the barbarians at last noticed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had Su Dingfang of Wuyi lead two hundred cavalry as vanguard. Riding through the fog, they were still seven li from the royal camp when the barbarians at last noticed them.

sentences.zh: 頡利乘千里馬先走，靖軍至，虜眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Jiali mounted a thousand-li horse and fled first; when Jing's army arrived, the barbarian masses broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali mounted a thousand-li horse and fled first; when Jing's army arrived, the barbarian masses broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 唐儉脫身得歸。

translations.literal: Tang Jian escaped and made it back.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian escaped and made it back alive.

sentences.zh: 靖斬首萬餘級，俘男女十餘萬，獲雜畜數十萬，殺隋義成公主，擒其子疊羅施。

translations.literal: Jing took more than ten thousand heads, captured more than one hundred thousand men and women, seized several hundred thousand assorted livestock, killed Princess Yicheng of Sui, and captured her son Die Luoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing took more than ten thousand heads, captured more than one hundred thousand men and women, seized several hundred thousand assorted livestock, killed Princess Yicheng of Sui, and captured her son Die Luoshi.

sentences.zh: 頡利帥萬餘人欲度磧，李世勣軍於磧口，頡利至，不得度，其大酋長皆帥眾降，世勣虜五萬餘口而還。

translations.literal: Jiali led more than ten thousand men wishing to cross the desert; Li Shiji stationed his army at the desert pass; when Jiali arrived he could not cross, and all his great chieftains led their followers in surrender; Shiji captured more than fifty thousand people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali led more than ten thousand men hoping to cross the desert. Li Shiji stationed his army at the desert pass; when Jiali arrived he could not cross, and all his great chieftains led their followers in surrender. Shiji captured more than fifty thousand people and returned.

sentences.zh: 斥地自陰山北至大漠，露布以聞。

translations.literal: They cleared land from Yinshan north to the great desert and reported the victory by proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: They cleared the land from Yinshan north to the great desert and reported the victory by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上還宮。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以克突厥赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, he declared a general amnesty throughout the realm for the conquest of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, he declared a general amnesty throughout the realm for the conquest of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫溫彥博為中書令，守侍中王珪為侍中；

translations.literal: He appointed Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo as Zhongshu Ling, and Acting Shizhong Wang Gui as Shizhong;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo as Zhongshu Ling, and Acting Shizhong Wang Gui as Shizhong;

sentences.zh: 守戶部尚書戴冑為戶部尚書，參預朝政；

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Revenue Dai Zhou as Minister of Revenue, to participate in court governance;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Minister of Revenue Dai Zhou as Minister of Revenue, to participate in court governance;

sentences.zh: 太常少卿蕭瑀為御史大夫，與宰臣參議朝政。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Ceremonies Xiao Yu as Censor-in-Chief, to consult with chief ministers on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Ceremonies Xiao Yu as Censor-in-Chief, to consult with chief ministers on court governance.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊辰，以突厥夾畢特勒阿史那思摩為右武修大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuchen, he appointed the Turk Jabi teghin Ashina Simo as General of the Right Military Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, he appointed the Turk Jabi teghin Ashina Simo as General of the Right Military Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 四夷君長詣闕請上為天可汗，上曰：「我為大唐天子，又下行可汗事乎？」

translations.literal: Chiefs of the four barbarians came to the court and asked that the emperor be titled Heavenly Qaghan. The emperor said: "I am Son of Heaven of Great Tang—shall I also perform the duties of a subordinate qaghan?"
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs of the four barbarians came to court and asked that the emperor be titled Heavenly Qaghan. The emperor said, "I am Son of Heaven of Great Tang—shall I also perform the duties of a subordinate qaghan?

sentences.zh: 群臣及四夷皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers and the four barbarians all cried "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers and the four barbarians all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 是後以璽書賜西北君長，皆稱天可汗。

translations.literal: Thereafter, in imperial seals sent to northwestern chiefs, they all addressed him as Heavenly Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, in imperial seals sent to northwestern chiefs, they all addressed him as Heavenly Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 庚午，突厥思結俟斤帥眾四萬來降。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Sijie irkin of the Turks led forty thousand followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Sijie irkin of the Turks led forty thousand followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以突利可汗為右衛大將軍、北平郡王。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, he appointed Tuli Qaghan as General of the Right Guard and Prince of Beiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he appointed Tuli Qaghan as General of the Right Guard and Prince of Beiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，始畢可汗以啟民母弟蘇尼失為沙缽羅設，督部落五萬家，牙直靈州西北。

translations.literal: Initially, Shibi Qaghan had appointed Qimin's younger brother Sunishi as Shabolu she, supervising fifty thousand households of tribes; his court was directly northwest of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Shibi Qaghan had appointed Qimin's younger brother Sunishi as Shabolu she, supervising fifty thousand tribal households; his court stood directly northwest of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及頡利政亂，蘇尼失所部獨不攜貳。

translations.literal: When Jiali's rule fell into disorder, Sunishi alone among those who had lost their divisions did not waver in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiali's rule fell into disorder, Sunishi alone among those who had lost their divisions did not waver in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 突利之來奔也，頡利立之為小可汗。

translations.literal: When Tuli had come fleeing to Tang, Jiali had established him as Lesser Qaghan.
