translations.idiomatic: When Tuli had fled to Tang, Jiali had established him as Lesser Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 及頡利敗走，往依之，將奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: When Jiali was defeated and fled, he went to rely on him, intending to flee to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiali was defeated and fled, he went to rely on him, intending to flee to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 大同道行軍總管任城王道宗引兵逼之，使蘇尼失執送頡利。

translations.literal: Area Commander of the Datong Circuit, Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, led troops to press him, and had Sunishi seize Jiali and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander of the Datong Circuit, Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, led troops to press him and had Sunishi seize Jiali and deliver him.

sentences.zh: 頡利以數騎夜走，匿於荒谷。

translations.literal: Jiali fled by night with a few horsemen and hid in a desolate valley.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali fled by night with a few horsemen and hid in a desolate valley.

sentences.zh: 蘇尼失懼，馳追獲之。

translations.literal: Sunishi, fearful, galloped in pursuit and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Sunishi, fearful, galloped in pursuit and captured him.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，行軍副總管張寶相帥眾奄至沙缽羅營，俘頡利送京師，蘇尼失舉眾來降，漠南之地遂空。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Deputy Area Commander Zhang Baoxiang led troops suddenly upon Shabolu's camp, captured Jiali and sent him to the capital; Sunishi led all his people in surrender, and the lands south of the desert were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Deputy Area Commander Zhang Baoxiang led troops suddenly upon Shabolu's camp, captured Jiali and sent him to the capital; Sunishi led all his people in surrender, and the lands south of the desert were emptied.

sentences.zh: 蔡成公杜如晦疾篤，上遣太子問疾，又自臨視之。

translations.literal: Duke Cheng of Cai, Du Ruhui, was gravely ill; the emperor sent the crown prince to inquire after his health, and also came personally to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng of Cai, Du Ruhui, was gravely ill; the emperor sent the crown prince to inquire after his health, and also came in person to visit him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，薨。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, he died.

sentences.zh: 上每得佳物，輒思如晦，遣使賜其家。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor obtained something fine, he would think of Ruhui and send an envoy to bestow it on his family.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor obtained something fine, he would think of Ruhui and send an envoy to bestow it on his family.

sentences.zh: 久之，語及如晦，必流涕，謂房玄齡曰：「公與如晦同佐朕，今獨見公，不見如晦矣！」

translations.literal: After a long time, whenever he spoke of Ruhui he would weep and say to Fang Xuanling: "You and Ruhui both aided me—now I see you alone and no longer see Ruhui!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, whenever he spoke of Ruhui he would weep and say to Fang Xuanling, "You and Ruhui both aided me—now I see you alone and no longer see Ruhui!"

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗至長安，夏，四月，戊戌，上御順天樓，盛陳文物，引見頡利，數之曰：「汝藉父兄之業，縱淫虐以取亡，罪一也；

translations.literal: Jiali Qaghan of the Turks reached Chang'an. In summer, the fourth month, on the day wuxu, the emperor ascended Shuntian Tower, displayed the realm's treasures in full array, and received Jiali, enumerating his offenses: "You relied on the work of your father and elder brother, indulged in lewdness and cruelty and brought ruin upon yourself—that is offense one;
translations.idiomatic: Jiali Qaghan of the Turks reached Chang'an. In summer, the fourth month, on wuxu, the emperor ascended Shuntian Tower, displayed the realm's treasures in full array, and received Jiali, enumerating his offenses: "You relied on the work of your father and elder brother, indulged in lewdness and cruelty and brought ruin upon yourself—that is offense one;

sentences.zh: 數與我盟而背之，二也；

translations.literal: you repeatedly made alliance with me and broke it—that is two;
translations.idiomatic: you repeatedly made alliance with me and broke it—that is two;

sentences.zh: 恃強好戰，暴骨如莽，三也；

translations.literal: relying on strength you loved warfare, and bones lay exposed like weeds—that is three;
translations.idiomatic: relying on strength you loved warfare, and bones lay exposed like weeds—that is three;

sentences.zh: 蹂我稼穡，掠我子女，四也；

translations.literal: you trampled our crops and plundered our people—that is four;
translations.idiomatic: you trampled our crops and plundered our people—that is four;

sentences.zh: 我宥汝罪，存汝社稷，而遷延不來，五也。

translations.literal: I pardoned your offenses and preserved your state, yet you delayed and did not come—that is five.
translations.idiomatic: I pardoned your offenses and preserved your state, yet you delayed and did not come—that is five.

sentences.zh: 然自便橋以來，不復大入為寇，以是得不死耳。」

translations.literal: Yet since Bianqiao you have not again made great raids as an invader—thereby you have barely escaped death."
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Bianqiao you have not again made great raids as an invader—thereby you have barely escaped death."

sentences.zh: 頡利哭謝而退。

translations.literal: Jiali wept in repentance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiali wept in repentance and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔館於太僕，厚廩食之。

translations.literal: An edict lodged him with the Grand Stable and generously supplied his food.
translations.idiomatic: An edict lodged him with the Grand Stable and generously supplied his food.

sentences.zh: 上皇聞擒頡利，歎曰：「漢高祖困白登，不能報；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor heard that Jiali had been captured and sighed: "Emperor Gaozu of Han was trapped at Baideng and could not retaliate;
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor heard that Jiali had been captured and sighed, "Emperor Gaozu of Han was trapped at Baideng and could not retaliate;

sentences.zh: 今我子能滅突厥，吾托付得人，復何憂哉！」

translations.literal: now my son has destroyed the Turks—I entrusted the realm to the right man; what further worry is there!"
translations.idiomatic: now my son has destroyed the Turks—I entrusted the realm to the right man; what further worry is there!"

sentences.zh: 上皇召上與貴臣十餘人及諸王、妃、主置酒凌煙閣，酒酣，上皇自彈琵琶，上起舞，公卿迭起為壽，逮夜而罷。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor summoned the emperor, more than ten high ministers, all the princes, consorts, and princesses, and set out wine at Lingyan Pavilion. When the wine was warm, the Retired Emperor himself played the pipa, the emperor danced, the ministers rose in turn to offer toasts, and the feast continued until night before ending.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor summoned the emperor, more than ten high ministers, all the princes, consorts, and princesses, and set out wine at Lingyan Pavilion. When the wine was warm, the Retired Emperor himself played the pipa, the emperor danced, the ministers rose in turn to offer toasts, and the feast continued until night before ending.

sentences.zh: 突厥既亡，其部落或北附薛延陀，或西奔西域，其降唐者尚十萬口，詔群臣議區處之宜。

translations.literal: Once the Turks had perished, some tribes submitted north to Xueyantuo, others fled west to the Western Regions; those who surrendered to Tang still numbered one hundred thousand people. An edict ordered the assembled ministers to debate how best to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turks had perished, some tribes submitted north to Xueyantuo, others fled west to the Western Regions; those who surrendered to Tang still numbered one hundred thousand people. An edict ordered the assembled ministers to debate how best to settle them.

sentences.zh: 朝士多言：「北狄自古為中國患，今幸而破亡，宜悉徙之河南兗、豫之間，分其種落，散居州縣，教之耕織，可以化胡虜為農民，永空塞北之地。」

translations.literal: Many court officials said: "The northern barbarians have been China's scourge since antiquity. Now that they are fortunately destroyed, all should be moved between the Yellow River south and Yan and Yu, their tribes divided and dispersed among prefectures and counties, taught to farm and weave—thus barbarian invaders can be turned into farmers and the northern frontier forever emptied."
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials said, "The northern barbarians have been China's scourge since antiquity. Now that they are fortunately destroyed, all should be moved between the Yellow River south and Yan and Yu, their tribes divided and dispersed among prefectures and counties, taught to farm and weave—thus barbarian invaders can be turned into farmers and the northern frontier forever emptied."

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎顏師古以為：「突厥、鐵勒皆上古所不能臣，陛下既得而臣之，請皆置之河北。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Shilang Yan Shigu held: "Both Turks and Tiele were peoples that antiquity could not subjugate. Your Majesty has already made them subjects—please settle them all north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Shilang Yan Shigu held, "Both Turks and Tiele were peoples that antiquity could not subjugate. Your Majesty has already made them subjects—please settle them all north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 分立酋長，領其部落，則永永無患矣。」

translations.literal: Appoint separate chiefs to lead their tribes, and there will never again be trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint separate chiefs to lead their tribes, and there will never again be trouble."

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李百藥以為：「突厥雖雲一國，然其種類區分，各有酋帥。

translations.literal: Libu Shilang Li Baiyao held: "Though the Turks are called one nation, their peoples are divided and each has its own chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Libu Shilang Li Baiyao held, "Though the Turks are called one nation, their peoples are divided and each has its own chieftain.

sentences.zh: 今宜因其離散，各即本部署為君長，不相臣屬；

translations.literal: Now we should take advantage of their dispersal and set up each original division as a separate chief, not subject to one another;
translations.idiomatic: Now we should take advantage of their dispersal and set up each original division as a separate chief, not subject to one another;

sentences.zh: 縱欲存立阿史那氏，唯可使臣其本族而已。

translations.literal: even if we wish to preserve the Ashina clan, we can only make them rulers over their own tribe alone.
translations.idiomatic: even if we wish to preserve the Ashina clan, we can only make them rulers over their own tribe alone.

sentences.zh: 國分則弱而易制，勢敵則難相吞滅，各自保全，必不能抗衡中國。

translations.literal: Split the state and it grows weak and easy to control; with rival powers equal, mutual destruction is hard—each will preserve itself and surely cannot stand against China.
translations.idiomatic: Split the state and it grows weak and easy to control; with rival powers equal, mutual destruction is hard—each will preserve itself and surely cannot stand against China.

sentences.zh: 仍請於定襄置都護府，為其節度，此安邊之長策也。」

translations.literal: He further requested establishing a Protectorate at Dingxiang to command them—this is the long-term policy for securing the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: He further requested establishing a Protectorate at Dingxiang to command them—this is the long-term policy for securing the frontier."

sentences.zh: 夏州都督竇靜以為：「戎狄之性，有如禽獸，不可以刑法威，不可以仁義教，況彼首丘之情，未易忘也。

translations.literal: Area Commander of Xia Prefecture Dou Jing held: "The nature of barbarians is like that of birds and beasts—they cannot be awed by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness; moreover, their longing for their native hills is not easily forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander of Xia Prefecture Dou Jing held, "The nature of barbarians is like that of birds and beasts—they cannot be awed by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness; moreover, their longing for their native hills is not easily forgotten.

sentences.zh: 置之中國，有損無益，恐一旦變生，犯我王略。

translations.literal: Settled within China, there is harm and no benefit—I fear that if rebellion arises suddenly, they will violate our royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Settled within China, there is harm and no benefit—I fear that if rebellion arises suddenly, they will violate our royal domain.

sentences.zh: 莫若因其破亡之餘，施以望外之恩，假之王侯之號，妻以宗室之女，分其土地，析其部落，使其權弱勢分，易為羈制，可使常為籓臣，永保邊塞。」

translations.literal: Better to take advantage of their ruin, bestow unexpected grace, grant them nominal titles of king and marquis, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their land and split their tribes, weaken their authority and scatter their strength so they are easy to tether and control—thus they can forever serve as frontier vassals and guard the border forever."
translations.idiomatic: Better to take advantage of their ruin, bestow unexpected grace, grant them nominal titles of king and marquis, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their land and split their tribes, weaken their authority and scatter their strength so they are easy to tether and control—thus they can forever serve as frontier vassals and guard the border forever."

sentences.zh: 溫彥博以為：「徙於兗、豫之間，則乖違物性，非所以存養之也。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo held: "Moving them to Yan and Yu would violate their nature—it is not the way to preserve and nurture them.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo held, "Moving them to Yan and Yu would violate their nature—it is not the way to preserve and nurture them.

sentences.zh: 請准漢建武故事，置降匈奴於塞下，全其部落，順其土俗，以實空虛之地，使為中國扞蔽，策之善者也。」

translations.literal: I request following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han, settling surrendered Xiongnu below the frontier, keeping their tribes intact and honoring their local customs, to fill empty lands and make them a shield for China—this is the wise policy."
translations.idiomatic: I request following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han, settling surrendered Xiongnu below the frontier, keeping their tribes intact and honoring their local customs, to fill empty lands and make them a shield for China—this is the wise policy."

sentences.zh: 魏徵以為：「突厥世為寇盜，百姓之仇也；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng held: "The Turks for generations have been raiders and plunderers—the enemies of the people;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng held, "The Turks for generations have been raiders and plunderers—the enemies of the people;

sentences.zh: 今幸而破亡，陛下以其降附，不忍盡殺，宜縱之使還故土，不可留之中國。

translations.literal: now that they are fortunately destroyed, Your Majesty, because they have surrendered, cannot bear to kill them all—you should release them to return to their homeland and not keep them within China.
translations.idiomatic: now that they are fortunately destroyed, Your Majesty, because they have surrendered, cannot bear to kill them all—you should release them to return to their homeland and not keep them within China.

sentences.zh: 夫戎狄人面獸心，弱則請服，強則叛亂，固其常性。

translations.literal: Barbarians have human faces but beastly hearts—when weak they beg submission, when strong they rebel; such is their constant nature.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians have human faces but beastly hearts—when weak they beg submission, when strong they rebel; such is their constant nature.

sentences.zh: 今降者眾近十萬，數年之後，蕃息倍多，必為腹心之疾，不可悔也。

translations.literal: Now the surrendered number nearly one hundred thousand; in several years they will multiply severalfold—they will surely become a malady in the heartland, and there will be no undoing it.
translations.idiomatic: Now the surrendered number nearly one hundred thousand; in several years they will multiply severalfold—they will surely become a malady in the heartland, and there will be no undoing it.

sentences.zh: 晉初諸胡與民雜居中國，郭欽、江統，皆勸武帝驅出塞外以絕亂階，武帝不從。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, various barbarians were mixed among the people within China; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier to cut off the seeds of disorder, but Emperor Wu did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin, various barbarians were mixed among the people within China; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier to cut off the seeds of disorder, but Emperor Wu did not listen.

sentences.zh: 後二十餘年，伊、洛之間，遂為氈裘之域，此前事之明鑒也！」

translations.literal: More than twenty years later, the lands between Yi and Luo became a domain of felt and fur—that is the clear mirror of events past!"
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years later, the lands between Yi and Luo became a domain of felt and fur—that is the clear mirror of events past!"

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「王者之於萬物。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "A true king toward all things—
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "A true king toward all things—

sentences.zh: 天覆地載，靡有所遺。

translations.literal: heaven covers and earth bears up; nothing is left out.
translations.idiomatic: heaven covers and earth bears up; nothing is left out.

sentences.zh: 今突厥窮來歸我，奈何棄之而不受乎！

translations.literal: Now the Turks, in their extremity, come to submit—how can we cast them away and not receive them!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Turks, in their extremity, come to submit—how can we cast them away and not receive them!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『有教無類。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'In teaching, there is no distinction of classes.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'In teaching, there is no distinction of classes.'

sentences.zh: 若救其死亡，授以生業，教之禮義，數年之後，悉為吾民。

translations.literal: If we save them from death, grant them livelihoods, and teach them ritual and righteousness, in several years they will all become our people.
translations.idiomatic: If we save them from death, grant them livelihoods, and teach them ritual and righteousness, in several years they will all become our people.

sentences.zh: 選其酋長，使入宿衛，畏威懷德，何後患之有！」

translations.literal: Select their chiefs to enter palace guard service—awed by our might and cherishing our virtue, what afterward trouble could there be!"
translations.idiomatic: Select their chiefs to enter palace guard service—awed by our might and cherishing our virtue, what afterward trouble could there be!"

sentences.zh: 上卒用彥博策，處突厥降眾，東自幽州，西至靈州；

translations.literal: The emperor finally adopted Yanbo's plan and settled the surrendered Turks from You Prefecture in the east to Ling Prefecture in the west;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally adopted Yanbo's plan and settled the surrendered Turks from You Prefecture in the east to Ling Prefecture in the west;

sentences.zh: 分突利故所統之地，置順、祐、化、長四州都督府；

translations.literal: he divided the territory formerly under Tuli's command and established four area command offices: Shun, You, Hua, and Chang;
translations.idiomatic: he divided the territory formerly under Tuli's command and established four area command offices: Shun, You, Hua, and Chang;

sentences.zh: 又分頡利之地為六州，左置定襄都督府，右置雲中都督府，以統其眾。

translations.literal: he also divided Jiali's territory into six prefectures, establishing the Dingxiang Area Command on the left and the Yunzhong Area Command on the right to govern the masses.
translations.idiomatic: he also divided Jiali's territory into six prefectures, establishing the Dingxiang Area Command on the left and the Yunzhong Area Command on the right to govern the masses.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛未，以突利為順州都督，使帥其部落之官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinwei, he appointed Tuli as Area Commander of Shun Prefecture, to lead the officials of his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinwei, he appointed Tuli as Area Commander of Shun Prefecture, to lead the officials of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「爾祖啟民挺身奔隋，隋立以為大可汗，奄有北荒，爾父始畢反為隋患。

translations.literal: The emperor admonished him: "Your ancestor Qimin threw himself into Sui's arms; Sui installed him as Great Qaghan and he briefly held the northern wilderness. Your father Shibi in turn became Sui's scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admonished him, "Your ancestor Qimin threw himself into Sui's arms; Sui installed him as Great Qaghan and he briefly held the northern wilderness. Your father Shibi in turn became Sui's scourge.

sentences.zh: 天道不容，故使爾今日亂亡如此。

translations.literal: Heaven's way brooks no such conduct—therefore it has brought you to ruin and disorder as you are today.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way brooks no such conduct—therefore it has brought you to ruin and disorder as you are today.

sentences.zh: 我所以不立爾為可汗者，懲啟民前事故也。

translations.literal: The reason I do not install you as qaghan is to punish the precedent set by Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I do not install you as qaghan is to punish the precedent set by Qimin.

sentences.zh: 今命爾為都督，爾宜善守國法，勿相侵掠，非徒欲中國久安，亦使爾宗族永全也！」

translations.literal: Now I appoint you as area commander. You should strictly observe the laws of the state and not plunder one another. It is not merely that I desire lasting peace for the Central Kingdom—it is also so that your clan and kindred may be preserved forever!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I appoint you area commander. You must strictly observe the laws of the state and refrain from raiding one another. I want not only lasting peace for the Central Kingdom, but also that your clan and kindred may endure in safety forever!"

sentences.zh: 壬申，以阿史那蘇尼失為懷德郡王，阿史那思摩為懷化郡王。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Ashina Sunishi was made Prince of Huai'de commandery, and Ashina Simo Prince of Huai'hua commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Ashina Sunishi was made Prince of Huai'de commandery and Ashina Simo Prince of Huai'hua commandery.

sentences.zh: 頡利之亡也，諸部落酋長皆棄頡利來降，獨思摩隨之，竟與頡利俱擒，上嘉其忠，拜右武候大將軍，尋以為北開州都督，使統頡利舊眾。

translations.literal: When Jieli fell, the chiefs of all the tribes abandoned Jieli and came to surrender; Simo alone followed him and in the end was captured together with Jieli. The emperor praised his loyalty, appointed him Grand General of the Right Wu-hou Guard, and soon made him Area Commander of Beikai Prefecture, entrusting him with Jieli's former followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli fell, the chiefs of all the tribes abandoned him and came over to Tang; Simo alone stayed with him and was captured along with Jieli. The emperor praised his loyalty, made him Grand General of the Right Wu-hou Guard, and soon appointed him area commander of Beikai Prefecture to lead Jieli's former followers.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以右武衛大將軍史大奈為豐州都督，其餘酋長至者，皆拜將軍、中郎將，布列朝廷，五品已上百餘人，殆與朝士相半，因而入居長安者近萬家。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, the Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guard Shi Danai was made Area Commander of Feng Prefecture. The other chiefs who arrived were all appointed generals and central court gentlemen and stationed throughout the court—more than a hundred of fifth rank and above, nearly half the court officials. Nearly ten thousand households consequently came to reside in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guard Shi Danai was made area commander of Feng Prefecture. The other chiefs who arrived were all appointed generals or central court gentlemen and posted at court—more than a hundred of fifth rank and above, nearly half the officials in attendance. Nearly ten thousand households consequently settled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔：「自今訟者，有經尚書省判不服，聽於東宮上啟，委太子裁決。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict: "From now on, in litigation, if after judgment by the Ministry of State Affairs one is still dissatisfied, appeal may be made to the Eastern Palace for the Crown Prince to decide.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, an edict declared, "From now on, if litigants remain dissatisfied after a ruling from the Ministry of State Affairs, they may appeal to the Eastern Palace and leave the decision to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 若仍不服，然後聞奏。」

translations.literal: If still dissatisfied, then report to the throne for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: If they were still dissatisfied, the matter would then be reported to the throne."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，御史大夫蕭瑀劾奏李靖破頡利牙帳，御軍無法，突厥珍物，虜掠俱盡，請付法司推科。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu impeached Li Jing for breaking Jieli's encampment—discipline in command of the army was lacking, and the Turks' precious goods were all plundered by the troops. He asked that the case be referred to the judicial authorities for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu impeached Li Jing for storming Jieli's encampment: army discipline had broken down, and the Turks' precious goods had been looted to the last item. He asked that the case be handed to the judicial authorities for investigation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 上特敕勿劾。

translations.literal: The emperor specially ordered that he not be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special order that the impeachment not proceed.

sentences.zh: 及靖入見，上大加責讓，靖頓首謝。

translations.literal: When Jing came for audience, the emperor severely rebuked him, and Jing kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing came to audience, the emperor rebuked him sharply, and Jing kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 久之，上乃曰：「隋史萬歲破達頭可汗，有功不賞，以罪致戮。

translations.literal: After some time, the emperor said, "In Sui, Shi Wansui broke the Qaghan Toutou—merit went unrewarded, and he was put to death for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: After a while, the emperor said, "Under the Sui, Shi Wansui defeated Qaghan Toutou—his merit went unrewarded, and he was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 朕則不然，錄公之功，赦公之罪。」

translations.literal: I am not like that—I record your merit and pardon your offense."
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that. I record your merit and pardon your offense."

sentences.zh: 加靖左光祿大夫，賜絹千匹，加真食邑通前五百戶。

translations.literal: He promoted Jing to Left Palace Officer of the Glory Emolument, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and added to his actual fief so that with previous holdings it totaled five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Jing to Left Palace Officer of the Glory Emolument, granted him a thousand bolts of silk, and added to his actual fief so that, together with his previous holdings, it totaled five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上謂靖曰：「前有人讒公，今朕意已寤，公勿以為懷。」

translations.literal: Before long, the emperor said to Jing, "Someone slandered you before; my mind is now clear—do not take it to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the emperor told Jing, "Someone slandered you before, but my mind is clear now—do not brood over it."

sentences.zh: 復賜絹二千匹。

translations.literal: He again granted two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He again granted him two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 林邑獻火珠，有司以其表辭不順，請討之，上曰：「好戰者亡，如隋煬帝、頡利可汗，皆耳目所親見也。

translations.literal: Lin Yi presented fire pearls; the relevant offices, finding their memorial's wording disrespectful, requested a punitive expedition. The emperor said, "Those who love war perish—Emperor Yang of Sui and Qaghan Jieli are both things we have seen with our own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi presented fire pearls. The relevant offices, finding the wording of their memorial disrespectful, requested a punitive expedition. The emperor said, "Those who love war perish—Emperor Yang of Sui and Qaghan Jieli are both before our very eyes.

sentences.zh: 小國勝之不武，況未可必乎！

translations.literal: It is unworthy to conquer a small state; moreover, success is not assured!
translations.idiomatic: To conquer a small state is unworthy, and success is hardly assured!

sentences.zh: 語言之間，何足介意！」

translations.literal: What is there to mind in turns of phrase!"
translations.idiomatic: What is there to mind in a turn of phrase!"

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，以阿史那蘇尼失為北寧州都督，以中郎將史善應為北撫州都督。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingyou, Ashina Sunishi was made Area Commander of Beining Prefecture, and Central Court Gentleman Shi Shanying Area Commander of Beifu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingyou, Ashina Sunishi was made area commander of Beining Prefecture, and Central Court Gentleman Shi Shanying area commander of Beifu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以右驍衛將軍康蘇密為北安州都督。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, General of the Right Xiao-wei Guard Kang Sumi was made Area Commander of Beian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, General of the Right Xiao-wei Guard Kang Sumi was made area commander of Beian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，發卒修洛陽宮以備巡幸，給事中張玄素上書諫，以為：「洛陽未有巡幸之期而預修宮室，非今日之急務。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, corvée laborers were dispatched to repair the Luoyang palace in preparation for an imperial tour. Supervising Secretary Zhang Xuansu submitted a memorial in remonstrance, arguing, "No date for touring Luoyang has been set, yet palace buildings are being repaired in advance—this is not today's urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, corvée laborers were sent to repair the Luoyang palace in preparation for an imperial tour. Supervising Secretary Zhang Xuansu submitted a memorial in remonstrance, arguing, "No date has been set for touring Luoyang, yet palace buildings are already being repaired—this is not an urgent task for today.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖納婁敬之說，自洛陽遷長安，豈非洛陽之地不及關中之形勝邪！

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han accepted Lou Jing's counsel and moved the capital from Luoyang to Chang'an—was it not because Luoyang's terrain was inferior to the strategic advantages of the Guanzhong region!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han accepted Lou Jing's counsel and moved the capital from Luoyang to Chang'an—was it not because Luoyang's terrain could not match the strategic advantages of Guanzhong!

sentences.zh: 景帝用晁錯之言而七國構禍，陛下今處突厥於中國，突厥之親，何如七國；

translations.literal: Emperor Jing followed Chao Cuo's advice and the Seven Kingdoms brought calamity. Your Majesty now houses the Turks within the Central Kingdom—the Turks' closeness, how does it compare with the Seven Kingdoms?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing followed Chao Cuo's advice and the Seven Kingdoms rose in rebellion. Your Majesty now houses the Turks within the Central Kingdom—how does their proximity compare with that of the Seven Kingdoms?

sentences.zh: 豈得不先為憂，而宮室可遽興，乘輿可輕動哉！

translations.literal: How can one fail to worry first, while palace buildings may be hastily raised and the imperial carriage lightly set in motion!
translations.idiomatic: How can one fail to worry first, while palace buildings are hastily raised and the imperial carriage is lightly set in motion!

sentences.zh: 臣見隋氏初營宮室，近山無大木，皆致之遠方，二千人曳一柱，以木為輪，則戛摩火出，乃鑄鐵為轂，行一二里，鐵彀輒破，別使數百人繼鐵彀隨而易之，盡日不過行二三十里，計一柱之費，已用數十萬功，則其餘可知矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that when the Sui first built palaces, there were no large trees near the mountains, so all were brought from afar. Two thousand men dragged a single pillar; wooden wheels were used, but friction produced fire, so iron hubs were cast instead. After traveling one or two li, the iron hubs would break, and several hundred men were separately assigned to follow with replacement iron hubs. In a whole day they advanced no more than twenty or thirty li. To calculate the cost of a single pillar already required hundreds of thousands of man-days of labor—the rest may be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has seen that when the Sui first built palaces, there were no large trees near the mountains, so timber had to be brought from afar. Two thousand men dragged a single pillar. Wooden wheels were tried, but friction set them ablaze, so iron hubs were cast instead. After one or two li, the iron hubs would break, and several hundred men had to follow with replacements. In a whole day they advanced no more than twenty or thirty li. A single pillar already cost hundreds of thousands of man-days of labor—the rest may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 陛下初平洛陽，凡隋氏宮室之宏侈者皆令毀之，曾未十年，復加營繕，何前日惡之而今日效之也！

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first pacified Luoyang, all the Sui palaces that were grand and extravagant were ordered destroyed. Not yet ten years have passed, and construction and repair are again underway—why did you hate it yesterday and imitate it today!
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first pacified Luoyang, all the Sui palaces that were grand and extravagant were ordered destroyed. Not ten years have passed, and construction and repair are underway again—why did you hate it yesterday and imitate it today!

sentences.zh: 且以今日財力，何如隋世！

translations.literal: Moreover, compared with the Sui age, how does today's financial strength stand!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, how does the empire's financial strength today compare with that of the Sui!

sentences.zh: 陛下役瘡痍之人，襲亡隋之弊，恐又甚於煬帝矣！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is employing a people covered in wounds and sores, repeating the failings of the fallen Sui—I fear this will exceed even Emperor Yang!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is employing a people still covered in wounds, repeating the failings of the fallen Sui—I fear this will exceed even Emperor Yang!"

sentences.zh: 上謂玄素曰：「卿謂我不如煬帝，何如桀、紂？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xuansu, "You say I am not the equal of Emperor Yang—what of Jie and Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Xuansu, "You say I am no better than Emperor Yang—what of Jie and Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若此役不息，亦同歸於亂耳。」

translations.literal: He replied, "If this labor does not cease, it will likewise end in disorder."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If this labor does not cease, the outcome will be disorder all the same."

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「吾思之不熟，乃至於是！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "I did not think this through carefully enough, and it has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "I did not think this through carefully enough, and it has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 顧謂房玄齡曰：「朕以洛陽土中，朝貢道均，意欲便民，故使營之。

translations.literal: He turned and said to Fang Xuanling, "I considered that Luoyang lies in the central plain and that tribute routes are evenly distributed; I intended to benefit the people, and therefore ordered construction.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Fang Xuanling and said, "I considered that Luoyang lies in the central plain and that tribute routes are evenly distributed; I meant to benefit the people, and therefore ordered construction.

sentences.zh: 今玄素所言誠有理，宜即為之罷役。

translations.literal: What Xuansu has said is truly reasonable; the labor should be halted at once.
translations.idiomatic: What Xuansu has said is truly reasonable. The labor should be halted at once.

sentences.zh: 後日或以事至洛陽，雖露居亦無傷也。」

translations.literal: If on some future day business brings me to Luoyang, even lodging in the open air will do no harm."
translations.idiomatic: If on some future day business brings me to Luoyang, even lodging in the open air will do no harm."

sentences.zh: 仍賜玄素彩二百匹。

translations.literal: He also granted Xuansu two hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted Xuansu two hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the cycle jiazi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day jiazi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，上問房玄齡、蕭瑀曰：「隋文帝何如主也？」

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the emperor asked Fang Xuanling and Xiao Yu, "What sort of ruler was Emperor Wen of Sui?"
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the emperor asked Fang Xuanling and Xiao Yu, "What sort of ruler was Emperor Wen of Sui?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「文帝勤於為治，每臨朝，或至日昃，五品已上，引坐論事，衛士傳餐而食；

translations.literal: They replied, "Emperor Wen was diligent in governance. Whenever he held court, he sometimes continued until the sun slanted westward. Officials of fifth rank and above were invited to sit and discuss affairs; guards passed out meals as they ate.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Emperor Wen was diligent in governance. Whenever he held court, he sometimes continued until the sun slanted westward. Officials of fifth rank and above were invited to sit and discuss affairs, while guards passed out meals as they ate.

sentences.zh: 雖性非仁厚，亦勵精之主也。」

translations.literal: Although by nature he was not generous and mild, he was nevertheless a ruler who strove with all his spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Although by nature he was not generous and mild, he was nevertheless a ruler who strove with all his spirit."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公得其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You have grasped one part and do not yet know the second.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have grasped one part and do not yet know the second.

sentences.zh: 文帝不明而喜察，不明則照有不通，喜察則多疑於物。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was unenlightened yet fond of close scrutiny. Unenlightened, his illumination did not reach everywhere; fond of scrutiny, he was excessively suspicious of things.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was unenlightened yet fond of close scrutiny. Unenlightened, his illumination did not reach everywhere; fond of scrutiny, he was excessively suspicious of things.

sentences.zh: 事皆自決，不任群臣。

translations.literal: He decided all affairs himself and did not entrust his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He decided all affairs himself and did not entrust his ministers.

sentences.zh: 天下至廣，一日萬機，雖復勞神苦形，豈能一一中理！

translations.literal: The realm is vast indeed, and in a single day ten thousand matters arise. Even if one exhausts spirit and wears down the body, how can every one be judged correctly!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast indeed, and in a single day ten thousand matters arise. Even if one exhausts spirit and wears down the body, how can every one be judged correctly!

sentences.zh: 群臣既知主意，唯取決受成，雖有愆違，莫敢諫爭，此所以二世而亡也。

translations.literal: Once the ministers knew the ruler's intent, they only accepted decisions already made. Even when there were faults and violations, none dared remonstrate or dispute. This is why the dynasty perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ministers knew the ruler's intent, they only accepted decisions already made. Even when there were faults and violations, none dared remonstrate or dispute. This is why the dynasty perished in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 朕則不然。

translations.literal: I am not like that.
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that.

sentences.zh: 擇天下賢才，置之百官，使思天下之事，關由宰相，審熟便安，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: I select the talented of the realm and place them among the hundred offices, so that they may think through the affairs of the realm. Matters pass through the chief ministers; once reviewed and found settled, they are then reported to me.
translations.idiomatic: I select the talented of the realm and place them among the hundred offices, so that they may think through the affairs of the realm. Matters pass through the chief ministers; once reviewed and found settled, they are then reported to me.

sentences.zh: 有功則賞，有罪則刑，誰敢不竭心力以修職業，何憂天下之不治乎！」

translations.literal: Merit is rewarded and guilt punished—who would not exhaust heart and strength in performing his duties? Why worry that the realm will not be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Merit is rewarded and guilt punished—who would not exhaust heart and strength in performing his duties? Why worry that the realm will not be well governed!"

sentences.zh: 因敕百司：「自今詔敕行下有未便者，皆應執奏，毋得阿從，不盡己意。」

translations.literal: He thereupon instructed the hundred offices, "From now on, whenever an edict or decree issued below proves inconvenient, all should firmly memorialize the throne and must not simply agree and follow, failing to speak their full mind."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon instructed the hundred offices, "From now on, whenever an edict or decree issued below proves inconvenient, all should firmly memorialize the throne and must not simply agree and follow, failing to speak their full mind."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以前太子少保李綱為太子少師，以兼御史大夫蕭瑀為太子少傅。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the former Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Li Gang was made Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and the concurrent Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the former Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Li Gang was made Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and the concurrent Censor-in-Chief Xiao Yu Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 李綱有足疾，上賜以步輿，使之乘至閣下，數引入禁中，問以政事。

translations.literal: Li Gang had an ailment of the foot; the emperor granted him a sedan chair and had him ride to the steps of the hall. He was repeatedly summoned into the inner palace and questioned on affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang had an ailment of the foot. The emperor granted him a sedan chair and had him ride to the steps of the hall. He was repeatedly summoned into the inner palace and questioned on affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 每至東宮，太子親拜之。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to the Eastern Palace, the Crown Prince personally bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to the Eastern Palace, the Crown Prince personally bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 太子每視事，上令綱與房玄齡侍坐。

translations.literal: Whenever the Crown Prince held audience, the emperor ordered Gang and Fang Xuanling to sit in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Crown Prince held audience, the emperor ordered Gang and Fang Xuanling to sit in attendance.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭瑀與宰相參議朝政，瑀氣剛而辭辯，房玄齡等皆不能抗，上多不用其言，玄齡、魏徵、溫彥博嘗有微過，瑀劾奏之，上竟不問。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yu joined the chief ministers in deliberating on court affairs. Yu was forceful in temperament and sharp in debate; Fang Xuanling and the others could not stand against him. The emperor often did not adopt his views. Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo had once committed minor faults, and Yu impeached them, but the emperor in the end did not inquire into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yu joined the chief ministers in deliberating on court affairs. Yu was forceful in temperament and sharp in debate; Fang Xuanling and the others could not stand against him. The emperor often did not adopt his views. Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo had once committed minor faults, and Yu impeached them, but the emperor in the end did not inquire into the matter.

sentences.zh: □瑀由此怏怏自失，遂罷御史大夫，為太子少傅，不復預聞朝政。

translations.literal: Yu thereby became resentful and dispirited. He was then removed as Censor-in-Chief and made Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, no longer taking part in deliberations on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, Yu became resentful and dispirited. He was then removed as Censor-in-Chief and made Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, no longer taking part in deliberations on court affairs.

sentences.zh: 西突厥種落散在伊吾，詔以涼州都督李大亮為西北道安撫大使，於磧口貯糧，來者賑給，使者招慰，相望於道。

translations.literal: Western Turkic tribes were scattered in Yiwu. An edict appointed Li Daliang, Area Commander of Liang Prefecture, Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit. Grain was stored at the desert passes; those who came were given relief. Envoys were sent to summon and reassure them, one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Western Turkic tribes were scattered in Yiwu. An edict appointed Li Daliang, area commander of Liang Prefecture, Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit. Grain was stored at the desert passes; those who came were given relief. Envoys were sent to summon and reassure them, one after another along the road.

sentences.zh: 大亮上言：「欲懷遠者必先安近，中國如本根，四夷如枝葉，疲中國以奉四夷，猶拔本根以益枝葉也。

translations.literal: Daliang submitted a memorial: "One who would win over the distant must first secure what is near. The Central Kingdom is like the root and trunk; the four barbarians are like branches and leaves. To exhaust the Central Kingdom in serving the four barbarians is like uprooting the root and trunk to nourish the branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang submitted a memorial: "One who would win over the distant must first secure what is near. The Central Kingdom is like the root and trunk; the four barbarians are like branches and leaves. To exhaust the Central Kingdom in serving the four barbarians is like uprooting the root and trunk to nourish the branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 臣遠考秦、漢，近觀隋室，外事戎狄，皆致疲弊。

translations.literal: Your subject, examining Qin and Han from afar and observing the Sui house at close hand, finds that external affairs with the Rong and Di all led to exhaustion and decline.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, examining Qin and Han from afar and observing the Sui house at close hand, finds that external affairs with the Rong and Di all led to exhaustion and decline.

sentences.zh: 今招致西突厥，但見勞費，未見其益。

translations.literal: Now in summoning the Western Turks, one sees only labor and expense, and has not yet seen the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Now in summoning the Western Turks, one sees only labor and expense, and has not yet seen the benefit.

sentences.zh: 況河西州縣蕭條，突厥微弱以來，始得耕獲；

translations.literal: Moreover, the prefectures and counties west of the Yellow River are desolate. Only since the Turks weakened have people begun to plow and harvest again.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prefectures and counties west of the Yellow River are desolate. Only since the Turks weakened have people begun to plow and harvest again.

sentences.zh: 今又供億此役，民將不堪，不若且罷招慰為便。

translations.literal: Now to supply and transport for this undertaking again—the people will be unable to bear it. It would be better for the time being to halt the summoning and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Now to supply and transport for this undertaking again—the people will be unable to bear it. It would be better for the time being to halt the summoning and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 伊吾之地，率皆沙磧，其人或自立君長，求稱臣內屬者，羈縻受之，使居塞外，為中國籓蔽，此乃施虛惠而收實利也。」

translations.literal: The lands of Yiwu are for the most part sandy desert. If some among the people set up their own chiefs and seek to declare themselves subjects and come within our fold, accept them under loose control, let them dwell beyond the passes, and make them a frontier screen for the Central Kingdom—this is to confer an empty favor and reap a real gain."
translations.idiomatic: The lands of Yiwu are for the most part sandy desert. If some among the people set up their own chiefs and seek to declare themselves subjects and come within our fold, accept them under loose control, let them dwell beyond the passes, and make them a frontier screen for the Central Kingdom—this is to confer an empty favor and reap a real gain."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午，詔以「常服未有差等，自今三品以上服紫，四品、五品服緋，六品、七品服綠，八品服青；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingwu, an edict declared, "Everyday dress has had no gradations in rank. From now on, those of third rank and above shall wear purple; fourth and fifth ranks, scarlet; sixth and seventh ranks, green; eighth rank, blue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingwu, an edict declared, "Everyday dress has had no gradations in rank. From now on, those of third rank and above shall wear purple; fourth and fifth ranks, scarlet; sixth and seventh ranks, green; eighth rank, blue.

sentences.zh: 婦人從其夫色。」

translations.literal: Women shall follow the color of their husbands."
translations.idiomatic: Women shall follow the color of their husbands."

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔以兵部尚書李靖為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, an edict appointed Li Jing, Minister of the Ministry of War, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, an edict appointed Li Jing, Minister of War, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 靖性沈厚，每與時宰參議，恂恂似不能言。

translations.literal: Jing was by nature deep and steady. Whenever he joined the chief ministers of the time in deliberation, he was deferential, as though unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was by nature deep and steady. Whenever he joined the chief ministers of the time in deliberation, he was deferential, as though unable to speak.

sentences.zh: 突厥既亡，營州都督薛萬淑遣契丹酋長貪沒折說諭東北諸夷，奚、■、室韋等十餘部皆內附。

translations.literal: The Turks having fallen, Xue Wanshu, Area Commander of Ying Prefecture, sent the Khitan chief Tanmozhe to persuade and instruct the various Yi of the northeast. More than ten tribes, including the Xi, Mohe, and Shiwei, all came within and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks having fallen, Xue Wanshu, area commander of Ying Prefecture, sent the Khitan chief Tanmozhe to persuade and instruct the various Yi of the northeast. More than ten tribes, including the Xi, Mohe, and Shiwei, all came within and submitted.

sentences.zh: 萬淑，萬均之兄也。

translations.literal: Wanshu was the elder brother of Wanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshu was the elder brother of Wanjun.

sentences.zh: 戊午，突厥欲谷設來降。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the Turk Yugushe came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Turk Yugushe came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 欲谷設，突利之弟也。

translations.literal: Yugushe was Tuli's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yugushe was Tuli's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 頡利敗，欲谷設奔高昌，聞突利為唐所禮，遂來降。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, Yugushe fled to Gaochang. Hearing that Tuli was treated with honor by Tang, he then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli was defeated, Yugushe fled to Gaochang. Hearing that Tuli was treated with honor by Tang, he then came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰，伊吾城主入朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuchen, the lord of Yiwu city came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuchen, the lord of Yiwu city came to court.

sentences.zh: 隋末，伊吾內屬，置伊吾郡；

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, Yiwu came within the fold and Yiwu commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui, Yiwu came within the fold and Yiwu commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，臣於突厥。

translations.literal: When Sui fell into disorder, it submitted to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui fell into disorder, it submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 頡利既滅，舉其屬七城來降，因以其地置伊西州。

translations.literal: When Jieli was destroyed, he brought all his dependents and seven cities to surrender, and on that account the land was made Yixi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli was destroyed, he brought all his dependents and seven cities to surrender, and on that account the land was made Yixi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思結部落饑貧，朔州刺史新豐張儉招集之，其不來者，仍居磧北，親屬私相往還，儉亦不禁。

translations.literal: The Sijie tribe was hungry and impoverished. Zhang Jian of Xinfeng, Prefect of Shuo Prefecture, summoned and gathered them. Those who did not come still dwelt north of the desert; kinsmen privately traveled back and forth, and Jian did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The Sijie tribe was hungry and impoverished. Zhang Jian of Xinfeng, prefect of Shuo Prefecture, summoned and gathered them. Those who did not come still dwelt north of the desert; kinsmen privately traveled back and forth, and Jian did not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 及儉徙勝州都督，州司奏思結將叛，詔儉往察之。

translations.literal: When Jian was transferred to be Area Commander of Sheng Prefecture, the prefectural offices reported that the Sijie were about to rebel. An edict ordered Jian to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was transferred to be area commander of Sheng Prefecture, the prefectural offices reported that the Sijie were about to rebel. An edict ordered Jian to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 儉單騎入其部落說諭，徙之代州，即以儉檢校代州都督，思結卒無叛者。

translations.literal: Jian entered their tribe alone on horseback to persuade and instruct them, then moved them to Dai Prefecture. Jian was at once made acting Area Commander of Dai Prefecture, and in the end none of the Sijie rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian entered their tribe alone on horseback to persuade and instruct them, then moved them to Dai Prefecture. Jian was at once made acting area commander of Dai Prefecture, and in the end none of the Sijie rebelled.

sentences.zh: 儉因勸之營田，歲大稔。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon encouraged them to open military colonies, and that year the harvest was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian thereupon encouraged them to open military colonies, and that year the harvest was abundant.

sentences.zh: 儉恐虜蓄積多，有異志，奏請和糴以充邊儲。

translations.literal: Jian feared that with the barbarians storing up much grain they might harbor other designs, and memorialized requesting government purchase at fair price to fill the frontier stores.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feared that with the barbarians storing up much grain they might harbor other designs, and memorialized requesting government purchase at fair price to fill the frontier stores.

sentences.zh: 部落喜，營田轉力，而邊備實焉。

translations.literal: The tribe rejoiced, the military colonies redoubled their effort, and the frontier defenses were thereby strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe rejoiced, the military colonies redoubled their effort, and the frontier defenses were thereby strengthened.

sentences.zh: 丙子，開南蠻地置費州、夷州。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, southern Man lands were opened and Fei Prefecture and Yi Prefecture were established.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, southern Man lands were opened and Fei Prefecture and Yi Prefecture were established.

sentences.zh: 己卯，上幸隴州。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the emperor visited Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, the emperor visited Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬辰，以右衛大將軍侯君集為兵部尚書，參議朝政。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day renchen, the Grand General of the Right Guard Hou Junji was made Minister of the Ministry of War and joined in deliberating on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on renchen, Grand General of the Right Guard Hou Junji was made Minister of War and joined in deliberating on court affairs.

sentences.zh: 甲子，車駕還京師，上讀《明堂針灸書》，云：「人五藏之系，鹹附於背。」

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital. The emperor read the Mingtang Acupuncture Classic, which says, "The systems of the human five viscera all have their attachments on the back."
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital. The emperor read the Mingtang Acupuncture Classic, which says, "The systems of the human five viscera all have their attachments on the back."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔自今毋得笞囚背。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, an edict declared that from now on prisoners must not be flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, an edict declared that from now on prisoners must not be flogged on the back.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，上獵於鹿苑；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiachen, the emperor hunted in the Deer Park.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, the emperor hunted in the Deer Park.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，高昌王麴文泰入朝。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, the King of Gaochang Qu Wentai came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the King of Gaochang Qu Wentai came to court.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國鹹欲因文泰使入貢，上遣文泰之臣厭怛紇干往迎之。

translations.literal: The various states of the Western Regions all wished to send tribute through Wentai's embassy. The emperor dispatched Wentai's minister Yandahigan to go and welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The various states of the Western Regions all wished to send tribute through Wentai's embassy. The emperor dispatched Wentai's minister Yandahigan to go and welcome them.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「昔光武不聽西域送侍子，置都護，以為不以蠻夷勞中國。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying, "Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han did not accept the Western Regions' sending of hostage princes or the establishment of a Protectorate, holding that one should not let the barbarians exhaust the Central Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying, "Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han did not accept the Western Regions' sending of hostage princes or the establishment of a Protectorate, holding that one should not let the barbarians exhaust the Central Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 今天下初定，前者文泰之來，所過勞費已甚，今借使十國入貢，其徒旅不減千人。

translations.literal: Today the realm has only just been settled. When Wentai came before, the labor and expense along the route were already extreme. If ten states were now to enter tribute through this embassy, their retinue would be no fewer than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm has only just been settled. When Wentai came before, the labor and expense along the route were already extreme. If ten states were now to enter tribute through this embassy, their retinue would be no fewer than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 邊民荒耗，將不勝其弊。

translations.literal: The frontier people are wasted and depleted—they will be unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier people are wasted and depleted—they will be unable to bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 若聽其商賈往來，與邊民交市，則可矣，倘以賓客遇之，非中國之利也。」

translations.literal: If merchants are allowed to come and go and trade with the frontier people, that will suffice. But if they are treated as honored guests, it is not to the Central Kingdom's advantage."
translations.idiomatic: If merchants are allowed to come and go and trade with the frontier people, that will suffice. But if they are treated as honored guests, it is not to the Central Kingdom's advantage."

sentences.zh: 時厭怛紇干已行，上遽令止之。

translations.literal: At that time Yandahigan had already set out; the emperor hurriedly ordered him halted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yandahigan had already set out; the emperor hurriedly ordered him halted.

sentences.zh: 諸宰相侍宴，上謂王珪曰：「卿識鑒精通，復善談論，玄齡以下，卿宜悉加品藻，且自謂與數子何如？」

translations.literal: The chief ministers attended a banquet. The emperor said to Wang Gui, "Your discernment is penetrating and you are also skilled in discussion. Below Xuanling and the rest—you should appraise them all, and say yourself how you compare with these several men?
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers attended a banquet. The emperor said to Wang Gui, "Your discernment is penetrating and you are also skilled in discussion. Below Xuanling and the rest—you should appraise them all, and say yourself how you compare with these several men?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「孜孜奉國，知無不為，臣不如玄齡。

translations.literal: [He] replied: "Diligently serving the state, knowing nothing that ought not be done—your subject is not the equal of Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In tirelessly serving the state and leaving nothing undone that ought to be done, I am no match for Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 才兼文武，出將入相，臣不如李靖。

translations.literal: Combining talent in both civil and military affairs, going out as a general and entering as a chancellor—your subject is not the equal of Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In uniting civil and military talent, commanding armies abroad and holding office at court, I cannot compare with Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 敷奏詳明，出納惟允，臣不如溫彥博。

translations.literal: Presenting memorials in thorough clarity, giving and receiving with fairness alone—your subject is not the equal of Wen Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: In drafting memorials with lucid detail and handling affairs with scrupulous fairness, I fall short of Wen Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 處繁治劇，眾務畢舉，臣不如戴冑。

translations.literal: Handling complexity and managing urgent affairs, completing all tasks—your subject is not the equal of Dai Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In managing complex and urgent business and seeing every task through, I am inferior to Dai Zhou.

sentences.zh: 恥君不及堯、舜，以諫爭為己任，臣不如魏徵。

translations.literal: Ashamed when the lord does not reach [the level of] Yao and Shun, taking remonstrance as one's own duty—your subject is not the equal of Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In feeling shame when the sovereign falls short of Yao and Shun and taking bold remonstrance as his charge, I cannot match Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 至於激濁揚清，嫉惡好善，臣於數子，亦有微長。」

translations.literal: As for stirring the turbid and elevating the pure, hating evil and loving good—among these several men your subject also has slight strengths."
translations.idiomatic: But when it comes to clarifying what is foul and elevating what is pure, hating wickedness and championing good, I do have modest strengths of my own among these men.

sentences.zh: 上深以為然，眾亦服其確論。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed, and the assembly also accepted his sound arguments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded, and everyone present respected the soundness of his analysis.

sentences.zh: 上之初即位也，嘗與群臣語及教化，上曰：「今承大亂之後，恐斯民未易化也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor had first ascended the throne, he once spoke with the ministers about transforming [the people] through instruction. The emperor said: "Now inheriting after great disorder, I fear these people will not be easy to transform."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had newly ascended the throne, he once discussed moral transformation with his ministers and said, "We have inherited the realm after great upheaval; I fear the people will not be easy to civilize.

sentences.zh: 魏徵對曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng replied: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 久安之民驕佚，驕佚則難教；

translations.literal: People long at peace grow arrogant and indulgent; when arrogant and indulgent, they are hard to instruct;
translations.idiomatic: People long settled in peace grow arrogant and lax, and the arrogant and lax are hard to teach;

sentences.zh: 經亂之民愁苦，愁苦則易化。

translations.literal: people who have passed through disorder are afflicted with sorrow; when afflicted with sorrow, they are easy to transform.
translations.idiomatic: while people who have endured disorder are worn down by hardship, and the worn and grieving are easy to transform.

sentences.zh: 譬猶饑者易為食，渴者易為飲也。」

translations.literal: It is like one who is hungry easily accepts food, one who is thirsty easily accepts drink."
translations.idiomatic: It is like the hungry who readily take food, or the thirsty who readily take drink.

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 封德彝非之曰：「三代以還，人漸澆訛，故秦任法律，漢雜霸道，蓋欲化而不能，豈能之而不欲邪！

translations.literal: Feng Deyi objected, saying: "Since the Three Dynasties, people have gradually grown dissolute and corrupt; therefore Qin relied on laws and statutes, Han mixed in hegemonic methods—probably they wished to transform but could not; how could they have been able yet not wished it!
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi objected, "Since the Three Dynasties, men have grown ever more dissolute and corrupt. That is why Qin turned to harsh laws and Han blended in hegemonic rule—they wanted to transform the people but could not. How could they have been able yet chosen not to!

sentences.zh: 魏徵書生，未識時務，若信其虛論，必敗國家。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng is a bookish scholar who does not understand the affairs of the age; if Your Majesty trusts his empty talk, he will surely ruin the state."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng is a bookish scholar who does not understand practical affairs. If Your Majesty trusts his idle theorizing, the state will surely come to ruin.

sentences.zh: 征曰：「五帝、三王不易民而化，昔黃帝征蚩尤，顓頊誅九黎，湯放桀，武王伐紂，皆能身致太平，豈非承大亂之後邪！

translations.literal: Zheng said: "The Five Emperors and Three Kings transformed the people without changing them. Formerly the Yellow Emperor campaigned against Chiyou, Zhuanxu executed the Nine Li, Tang exiled Jie, King Wu attacked Zhou—each in person brought about great peace; were these not cases of inheriting after great disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "The Five Emperors and Three Kings civilized their people without displacing them. The Yellow Emperor campaigned against Chiyou; Zhuanxu put down the Nine Li; Tang exiled Jie; King Wu overthrew Zhou—all brought peace in their own day. Were these not successors to ages of chaos?

sentences.zh: 若謂古人淳樸，漸至澆訛，則至於今日，當悉化為鬼魅矣，人主安得而治之！」

translations.literal: If one says the ancients were simple and unsophisticated and gradually arrived at dissoluteness and corruption, then by today they should all have transformed into demons and goblins—how could a ruler govern them!"
translations.idiomatic: If we say antiquity was pure and only later turned corrupt, then by now humanity ought to have become nothing but demons—how could any ruler govern such a people!

sentences.zh: 上卒從征言。

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed Zheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor adopted Wei Zheng's view.

sentences.zh: 元年，關中饑，米斗直絹一匹；

translations.literal: In the first year, Guanzhong suffered famine; a dou of rice was worth one bolt of silk;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year Guanzhong suffered famine, and a peck of rice cost a full bolt of silk;

sentences.zh: 二年，天下蝗；

translations.literal: in the second year, locusts [afflicted] the empire;
translations.idiomatic: in the second year locusts devastated the realm;

sentences.zh: 三年，大水。

translations.literal: in the third year, great floods.
translations.idiomatic: and in the third year came catastrophic floods.

sentences.zh: 上勤而撫之，民雖東西就食，未嘗嗟怨。

translations.literal: The emperor worked diligently to comfort them; though the people went east and west seeking food, they never sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worked tirelessly to succor them; though people wandered east and west in search of food, none were heard to murmur in complaint.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下大稔，流散者鹹歸鄉里，米鬥不過三、四錢，終歲斷死刑才二十九人。

translations.literal: That year the empire had a great harvest; those who had been scattered all returned to their home districts. A dou of rice did not exceed three or four cash, and death sentences for the whole year totaled only twenty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire enjoyed a bountiful harvest; the displaced all returned home; a peck of rice cost no more than three or four cash; and only twenty-nine executions were carried out all year.

sentences.zh: 東至於海，南及五嶺，皆外戶不閉，行旅不繼糧，取給於道路焉。

translations.literal: East to the sea, south to the Five Ridges—all outside doors were left unbarred; travelers did not carry provisions in succession but obtained supplies on the road.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern sea to the southern Five Ridges, outer gates stood unbarred; travelers needed no provisions of their own and could take what they needed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 上謂長孫無忌曰：「貞觀之初，上書者皆云：『人主當獨運威權，不可委之臣下。』

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhangsun Wuji: "In the early Zhenguan reign, those who submitted memorials all said: 'The ruler ought alone to wield authority and power; it must not be delegated to ministers below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Zhangsun Wuji, "Early in the Zhenguan reign, memorial writers all argued that the sovereign should wield authority alone and never delegate it to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 又云：『宜震耀威武，征討四夷。』

translations.literal: They also said: 'One ought to display awesome martial might and campaign against the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They also urged that we should display martial might and launch campaigns against the four frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 唯魏徵勸朕『偃武修文，中國既安，四夷自服。』

translations.literal: Only Wei Zheng advised me: 'Lay down arms and cultivate culture; once the Central Lands are at peace, the four barbarians will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei Zheng counseled me to 'sheath the sword and cultivate civil order—once the heartland is secure, the four quarters will submit of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 朕用其言。

translations.literal: I employed his words.
translations.idiomatic: I followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 今頡利成擒，其酋長並帶刀宿衛，部落皆襲衣冠，征之力也，但恨不使封德彝見之耳！」

translations.literal: Now Jieli has been captured; his chieftains all wear swords at court as palace guards; the tribes all adopt caps and robes. This is Zheng's achievement—only I regret that Feng Deyi was not made to see it!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jieli has been taken, his chieftains serve at court with swords at their belts, and his tribes have adopted Chinese dress. That is Wei Zheng's doing—and I only regret that Feng Deyi did not live to see it!

sentences.zh: 征再拜謝曰：「突厥破滅，海內康寧，皆陛下威德，臣何力焉！」

translations.literal: Zheng bowed twice in thanks and said: "The destruction of the Turks and peace within the seas—all is Your Majesty's awesome virtue; what strength has your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng bowed twice and demurred, "The fall of the Turks and peace across the realm are Your Majesty's sovereign power and virtue—what part did I play in that!

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕能任公，公能稱所任，則其功豈獨在朕乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I was able to employ you; you were able to fulfill what you were entrusted with—then is the achievement yours alone, or mine alone!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I was able to place my trust in you, and you were able to honor that trust—so how can the credit belong to me alone?"

sentences.zh: 房玄齡奏：「閱府庫甲兵，遠勝隋世。」

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling memorialized: "On inspection of the armory stores of armor and weapons, they far surpass the Sui age."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling reported, "I have reviewed the armory, and our stock of armor and weapons far exceeds what the Sui possessed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「甲兵武備，誠不可闕；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Armor, weapons, and martial preparedness indeed must not be wanting;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Armor, arms, and military preparedness must not be neglected;

sentences.zh: 然煬帝甲兵豈不足邪！

translations.literal: yet were Emperor Yang's armor and weapons not sufficient!
translations.idiomatic: yet was Emperor Yang's arsenal not amply stocked!

sentences.zh: 卒亡天下。

translations.literal: In the end he lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 若公等盡力，使百姓乂安，此乃朕之甲兵也。」

translations.literal: If you and the rest exert your strength and make the common people secure and at peace, this is my armor and weapons."
translations.idiomatic: If all of you give your utmost so that the people live in peace and safety, that will be my true armor and arms."

sentences.zh: 上謂秘書監蕭璟曰：「卿在隋世數見皇后乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Secretary Director Xiao Jing: "In Sui times did you several times see the empress?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Secretary Director Xiao Jing, "In Sui times, did you ever see the empress on more than one occasion?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「彼兒女且不得見，臣何人，得見之？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Even the emperor's own sons and daughters could not see her—what sort of person is your subject that he could see her?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Even the emperor's own children were not permitted to see her—who am I, that I should have been allowed to?

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「臣聞煬帝不信齊王，恆有中使察之，聞其宴飲，則曰『彼營何事得遂而喜！』

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "Your subject has heard that Emperor Yang did not trust the Prince of Qi—there were always palace envoys observing him. When they heard he was feasting and drinking, they would say, 'What scheme of his has succeeded that makes him rejoice!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "I have heard that Emperor Yang did not trust the Prince of Qi and kept palace agents spying on him. If they learned he was feasting, they would say, 'What plot has succeeded to make him so merry!

sentences.zh: 聞其憂悴，則曰『彼有他念故爾。』

translations.literal: When they heard he was grief-stricken and haggard, they would say, 'He has other intentions for being thus.
translations.idiomatic: If they learned he was haggard with worry, they would say, 'He must be harboring other designs—that is why he looks so wretched.

sentences.zh: 父子之間且猶如是，況他人乎！」

translations.literal: Between father and son it was still thus—how much more so for others!"
translations.idiomatic: Even between father and son distrust ran so deep—what hope was there for anyone else!

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「朕今視楊政道，勝煬帝之於齊王遠矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Today in my regard for Yang Zhengdao, I am far superior to Emperor Yang's treatment of the Prince of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "In how I treat Yang Zhengdao today I am far ahead of Emperor Yang's treatment of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 璟，瑀之兄也。

translations.literal: Jing was Yu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jing was the elder brother of Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 西突厥肆葉護可汗既先可汗之子，為眾所附，莫賀咄可汗所部酋長多歸之，肆葉護引兵擊莫賀咄，莫賀咄兵敗，逃於金山，為泥熟設所殺，諸部共推肆葉護為大可汗。

translations.literal: The Western Turkic Shaboluo Khan, being the son of the previous khan, was attached to by the masses; many chieftains of Khan Moheduo's divisions submitted to him. Shaboluo led troops to attack Moheduo; Moheduo's army was defeated; he fled to Mount Jin and was killed by the Nishou Commander; the various divisions together installed Shaboluo as Great Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluo, khan of the Western Turks, was the late khan's son and won broad allegiance. Many of Moheduo Khan's chieftains went over to him. Shaboluo marched against Moheduo, routed his forces, and pursued him to Mount Jin, where the Nishoushe commander killed him; the tribes then jointly raised Shaboluo to great khan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，詔僧、尼、道士致拜父母。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: an edict [ordered that] monks, nuns, and Daoist priests should bow to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, an edict required Buddhist monks and nuns and Daoist priests to bow to their parents.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上大獵於昆明池，四夷君長鹹從。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou the emperor greatly hunted at Kunming Pond; the chieftains of the four barbarians all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor held a grand hunt at Kunming Pond, with chieftains from the four quarters in attendance.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，宴高昌王文泰及群臣。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu he feasted King Wen Tai of Gaochang and the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he banqueted King Wen Tai of Gaochang along with his ministers.

sentences.zh: 丙子，還宮，親獻禽於大安宮。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi he returned to the palace and personally presented game to the Great Peace Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he returned to the palace and personally presented his quarry to the retired emperor at Dayan Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸未，朝集使趙郡王孝恭等上表，以四夷鹹服，請封禪；

translations.literal: On the day guiwei the assembly envoys, the Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong and others, submitted a memorial that since the four barbarians all submitted, they requested a feng and shan ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the provincial assembly envoys, led by Prince Li Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery, submitted a memorial noting that the four quarters had all submitted and requesting a Feng and Shan ritual;

sentences.zh: 上手詔不許。」

translations.literal: the emperor by hand edict did not grant it."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor personally wrote back to decline."

sentences.zh: 有司上言皇太子當冠，用二月吉，請追兵備儀仗。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that the crown prince should receive capping, using an auspicious day in the second month, and requested the summoning of troops, equipment, and ceremonial insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported that the crown prince was due for capping on an auspicious day in the second month and asked that troops and ceremonial regalia be mobilized.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「東作方興，宜改用十月。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Eastern-field labor is just beginning; it is fitting to change to the tenth month."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Spring planting is just getting under way; we should move the ceremony to the tenth month instead.

sentences.zh: 少傅蕭瑀奏：「據陰陽書不若二月。」

translations.literal: Junior Tutor Xiao Yu memorialized: "According to the yin-yang books, the second month is better."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor Xiao Yu argued that according to the almanacs of yin and yang, the second month was the better choice.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吉凶在人。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Auspicious and inauspicious [affairs] lie in men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Good fortune and ill depend on men, not omens.

sentences.zh: 若動依陰陽，不顧禮義，吉可得乎！

translations.literal: If one acts according to yin and yang and does not heed ritual and righteousness, can auspiciousness be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: If we act by yin-yang charts and ignore ritual duty, how can we expect good fortune!

sentences.zh: 循正而行，自與吉會。

translations.literal: Following the upright path in action, one naturally meets with auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Do what is right, and good fortune will follow of itself.

sentences.zh: 農時最急，不可失也。」

translations.literal: The agricultural season is most urgent and must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: The farming season is what matters most—we cannot afford to miss it."

sentences.zh: 二月，甲辰，詔：「諸州有京觀處，無問新舊，宜悉剷削，加土為墳，掩蔽枯朽，勿令暴露。」

translations.literal: Second month, on the day jiachen, an edict: "Wherever in the provinces there are jingguan [battle mounds], regardless of new or old, all should be fully leveled; add earth to make burial mounds, cover and hide the withered bones, and do not let them be exposed."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiachen, an edict ordered: "Wherever in the provinces battlefield mounds stand, old or new, they are to be leveled; earth is to be heaped into proper graves, the bones decently covered, and nothing left exposed to the elements."

sentences.zh: 己酉，封皇弟元裕為鄶王，元名為譙王，靈夔為魏王，元祥為許王，元曉為密王。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou imperial younger brother Yuan Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Kuai, Yuan Ming as Prince of Qiao, Lingkui as Prince of Wei, Yuan Xiang as Prince of Xu, Yuan Xiao as Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Yuan Yu as Prince of Kuai, Yuan Ming as Prince of Qiao, Lingkui as Prince of Wei, Yuan Xiang as Prince of Xu, and Yuan Xiao as Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，封皇子愔為梁王，惲為郯王，貞為漢王，治為晉王，慎為申王，囂為江王，簡為代王。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu the princes Yin were enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, Yun as Prince of Tan, Zhen as Prince of Han, Zhi as Prince of Jin, Shen as Prince of Shen, Xiao as Prince of Jiang, Jian as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor's sons were enfeoffed: Yin as Prince of Liang, Yun as Prince of Tan, Zhen as Prince of Han, Zhi as Prince of Jin, Shen as Prince of Shen, Xiao as Prince of Jiang, and Jian as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬辰，代王簡薨。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the day renchen, Prince Jian of Dai died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Jian of Dai died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，靈州斛薛叛，任城王道宗等追擊，破之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin the Huxue at Lingzhou rebelled; the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong and others pursued and attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Huxue tribe at Lingzhou rebelled; Li Daozong, Prince of Rencheng, pursued them and routed their forces.

sentences.zh: 隋末，中國人多沒於突厥，及突厥降，上遣使以金帛贖之。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, many people of the Central Lands were lost to the Turks; when the Turks submitted, the emperor sent envoys to redeem them with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui many Chinese had been taken captive by the Turks. When the Turks submitted, the emperor sent envoys to ransom them with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙丑，有司奏，凡得男女八萬口。
