translations.literal: Fifth month, on the day yichou, the responsible offices reported that in total eighty thousand men and women were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yichou, the relevant offices reported that eighty thousand men and women had been recovered in all.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲寅，太子少師新昌貞公李綱薨。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the day jiayin, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Duke Zhen of Xinchang, Li Gang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiayin, Li Gang, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Duke Zhen of Xinchang, died.

sentences.zh: 初，周齊王憲女，孀居無子，綱贍恤甚厚。

translations.literal: Previously the daughter of Northern Zhou Prince of Qi Xian, widowed without sons, Li Gang supported and comforted [her] very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the widow of Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi of Northern Zhou, who had no children, had been supported with great generosity by Li Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱薨，其女以父禮喪之。

translations.literal: When Gang died, her daughter mourned him with the rites due a father.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang died, she observed mourning for him as for a father.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲辰，遣使詣高麗，收隋氏戰亡骸骨，葬而祭之。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on the day jiachen, envoys were dispatched to Goguryeo to collect the bones of those killed in Sui campaigns, bury them, and offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on jiachen, envoys were sent to Goguryeo to recover the remains of Sui soldiers who had fallen in battle, bury them, and perform rites of mourning.

sentences.zh: 河內人李好德得心疾，妄為妖言，詔按其事。

translations.literal: Li Haode of Henei suffered a heart affliction and uttered reckless demonic talk; an edict ordered investigation of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haode of Henei, afflicted by mental illness, spoke wild and seditious words; the emperor ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 大理丞張蘊古奏：「好德被疾有征，法不當坐。」

translations.literal: Grand Court of Revision Assistant Zhang Yungu memorialized: "Haode's affliction has clear signs; by law he should not be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Yungu reported that Haode's illness was clearly documented and that the law did not warrant punishment.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀劾奏：「蘊古貫在相州，好德之兄厚德為其刺史，情在阿縱，按事不實。」

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Quan Wanji impeached: "Yungu was once stationed in Xiangzhou, where Haode's elder brother Houde was its prefect—the sentiment was partial indulgence; the investigation was not factually grounded."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Quan Wanji impeached Zhang Yungu, arguing that while serving in Xiang Prefecture Yungu had favored Haode because Haode's elder brother Houde was prefect there and had therefore whitewashed the case.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命斬之於市，既而悔之，因詔：「自今有死罪，雖令即決，仍三覆奏乃行刑。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him executed in the market; afterward he regretted it, and therefore edicted: "From today on, for death sentences, even if ordered for immediate decision, still require three repeated memorial submissions before carrying out execution."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, ordered Zhang Yungu executed in public. He soon regretted it and issued an edict: "Henceforth, even when a capital sentence is ordered for immediate execution, three memorial reviews must still be completed before the sentence is carried out."

sentences.zh: 權萬紀與侍御史李仁發，俱以告訐有寵於上，由是諸大臣數被譴怒。

translations.literal: Quan Wanji and Censor Li Renfa both had favor with the emperor through informing and denouncing; thereby the chief ministers were repeatedly reprimanded in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wanji and Censor Li Renfa both won the emperor's favor through accusation and denunciation, and on that account senior ministers were repeatedly rebuked.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「萬紀等小人，不識大體，以訐為直，以讒為忠。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Wanji and such petty men do not understand the larger pattern; they take informing as uprightness and slander as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated, "Wanji and men like him are petty creatures who grasp neither the larger interest nor the proper bounds of counsel—they treat informing as integrity and slander as loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下非不知其無堪，蓋取其無所避忌，欲以警策群臣耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is not unaware of their unfitness—probably you chose them for their lack of scruple, wishing to warn and spur the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is not unaware of their unfitness; you chose them because they hold nothing back, hoping thereby to keep the court alert.

sentences.zh: 而萬紀等挾恩依勢，逞其奸謀，凡所彈射，皆非有罪。

translations.literal: Yet Wanji and the rest, relying on favor and leaning on power, have given free rein to their wicked schemes; all they have impeached are not [people who] have offenses.
translations.idiomatic: But Wanji and his like, trading on imperial favor, have abused their position; every target they have attacked was innocent.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱未能舉善以厲俗，奈何暱奸以自損乎！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, even if unable to promote the good to reform custom—how can you draw close to the wicked and harm yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty cannot yet elevate the virtuous to reform the realm, why embrace schemers and harm your own rule!

sentences.zh: 上默然，賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 久之，萬紀等奸狀自露，皆得罪。

translations.literal: After a long while, Wanji and the rest's wicked conduct exposed itself; all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In time Wanji and his associates' misconduct came to light, and all were punished.

sentences.zh: 九月，上修仁壽宮，更命曰九成宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the emperor repaired Renshou Palace and renamed it Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor restored Renshou Palace and renamed it Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 又將修洛陽宮，民部尚書戴冑表諫，以「亂離甫爾，百姓凋弊，帑藏空虛，若營造不已，公私勞費，殆不能堪！」

translations.literal: Also about to repair Luoyang Palace—Minister of the Population Dai Zhou submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Disorder and separation have just ceased; the common people are exhausted and impoverished, the treasury is empty. If construction goes on without end, public and private labor and expense will scarcely be endurable!"
translations.idiomatic: He was also planning to restore Luoyang Palace. Minister of Revenue Dai Zhou remonstrated in a memorial: "We have only just emerged from chaos; the people are destitute and the treasury empty. If construction continues without end, the burden on public and private resources will become unbearable!

sentences.zh: 上嘉之曰：「戴冑於我非親，但以忠直體國，知無不言，故以官爵酬之耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised him, saying: "Dai Zhou is no kinsman of mine—only because he is loyal and upright in embodying the state, knowing nothing he will not speak, therefore I reward him with office and rank."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, saying, "Dai Zhou is no kinsman of mine; I reward him with office only because he serves the realm with blunt loyalty and speaks without holding back.

sentences.zh: 久之，竟命將作大匠竇璡修洛陽宮，璡鑿池築山，雕飾華靡。

translations.literal: After a long while, in the end he ordered Master of Works Dou Jin to repair Luoyang Palace; Jin excavated pools and built mountains, carved ornamentation lavish and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, however, he ordered Master of Works Dou Jin to proceed with Luoyang Palace. Jin dug ornamental lakes, piled up artificial mountains, and lavished the work with extravagant decoration.

sentences.zh: 上遽命毀之，免璡官。

translations.literal: The emperor hastily ordered it destroyed and removed Jin from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the work demolished and dismissed Jin from office.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，上逐兔於後苑，左領軍將軍執失思力諫曰：「天命陛下為華、夷父母，奈何自輕！」

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on the day bingwu, the emperor chased hares in the rear park; Left Palace Guard General Zhishi Sili remonstrated: "Heaven mandated Your Majesty as parent to Chinese and barbarians alike—how can you slight yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu the emperor was hunting hares in the rear park. Left Palace Guard General Ashina Simi remonstrated, "Heaven has made Your Majesty the father and mother of Chinese and barbarian alike—why treat your life so lightly!

sentences.zh: 上又將逐鹿，思力脫巾解帶，跪而固諫，上為之止。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to chase deer again; Sili removed his headcloth and loosened his belt, knelt and firmly remonstrated; the emperor stopped on his account.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to hunt deer again, Simi stripped off his headcloth, loosened his belt, knelt in blocking remonstrance, and the emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 初，上令群臣議封建，魏徵議以為：「若封建諸侯，則卿大夫鹹資俸祿，必致厚斂。

translations.literal: Initially the emperor ordered the ministers to discuss enfeoffment of feudal lords. Wei Zheng argued: "If feudal lords are enfeoffed, then the high and middle officials all rely on salaries and stipends and will surely lead to heavy taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered a court debate on restoring feudal enfeoffment. Wei Zheng argued that if territorial lords were enfeoffed, their officials would all depend on salaries drawn from the domain and would inevitably resort to heavy taxation.

sentences.zh: 又，京畿賦稅不多，所資畿外，若盡以封國邑，經費頓闕。

translations.literal: Further, the capital region's taxes and levies are not many; what it relies on is from outside the capital district—if all are used to enfeoff state territories, expenditures will suddenly be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, tax revenues from the capital district are limited; the court relies on levies from the provinces. If those territories were all carved into feudal domains, state finances would collapse overnight.

sentences.zh: 又，燕、秦、趙、代俱帶外夷，若有警急，追兵內地，難以奔赴。」

translations.literal: Further, Yan, Qin, Zhao, and Dai all border on outer barbarians; if there is urgent alarm, pursuing troops from the interior is hard to dispatch in time."
translations.idiomatic: Further, Yan, Qin, Zhao, and Dai all border foreign peoples. In an emergency, troops would have to be summoned from the interior, and they could not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李百藥以為：「運祚修短，定命自天，堯、舜大聖，守之而不能固；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Baiyao argued: "The length of a dynasty's fortune is fated by Heaven; Yao and Shun, greatly sage, guarded it yet could not hold it fast;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Baiyao argued that the rise and fall of dynasties is Heaven's decree: Yao and Shun, sublime sages though they were, could not preserve their line forever;

sentences.zh: 漢、魏微賤，拒之而不能卻。

translations.literal: Han and Wei, of humble origin, resisted it yet could not repel it.
translations.idiomatic: while Han and Wei, born in humble station, resisted feudalism yet could not drive it away.

sentences.zh: 今使勳戚子孫皆有民有社，易世之後，將驕淫自恣，攻戰相殘，害民尤深，不若守令之迭居也。」

translations.literal: Now if meritorious kinsmen's descendants all have people and altars, after generations change they will grow arrogant, dissolute, and unrestrained, attacking and battling one another—harming the people especially deeply. It is not like the succession of prefects and magistrates."
translations.idiomatic: If we now grant meritorious kinsmen peoples and domain altars, their descendants will grow arrogant and predatory, war on one another, and inflict far worse harm on the common people than the rotation of appointed prefects and magistrates ever could.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎顏師古以為：「不若分王諸子，勿令過大，間以州縣，雜錯而居，互相維持，使各守其境，協力同心，足扶京室；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu argued: "Better to divide and enfeoff the sons as kings, not letting [their domains] be too large, interspersing with prefectures and counties, living mixed and interlocking, mutually sustaining one another—each guarding his territory, joining strength with one heart, sufficient to support the capital house;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu favored dividing the princes into smaller domains intermixed with prefectures and counties, mutually supporting one another so that each guarded his territory, acted in concert, and buttressed the throne;

sentences.zh: 為置官寮，皆省司選用，法令之外，不得擅作威刑，朝貢禮儀，具為條式。

translations.literal: appoint official staffs for them—all selected and employed by the provincial offices; outside the laws and ordinances they must not on their own impose authority and punishments; court tribute and ceremonial rites should all be laid out in regulations.
translations.idiomatic: each domain would be staffed with officials appointed by the central ministries, forbidden to impose punishments beyond the code, and bound by detailed regulations governing tribute and court ritual.

sentences.zh: 一定此制，萬代無虞。」

translations.literal: Once this system is established, for myriad generations there will be no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Establish this system once, and future ages need never worry.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，詔：「皇家宗室及勳賢之臣，宜令作鎮籓部，貽厥子孫，非有大故，無或黜免，所司明為條列，定等級以聞。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen, an edict stated: "Members of the imperial clan and meritorious worthy ministers should be made to guard frontier provinces, bequeathing [positions] to their descendants; unless there is great cause, none may be dismissed or removed. The responsible offices should clearly set forth regulations, fix ranks and grades, and report."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, an edict proclaimed: "Imperial clansmen and meritorious ministers shall be posted to guard frontier provinces, with positions inherited by their descendants. None may be removed except for grave cause. The relevant ministries shall draft detailed regulations, establish rank grades, and report them."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，林邑獻五色鸚鵡，丁卯，新羅獻美女二人；

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Linyi presented a five-colored parrot; on the day dingmao, Silla presented two beautiful women;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Linyi presented a multicolored parrot; on dingmao, Silla sent two beautiful women as tribute;

sentences.zh: 魏徵以為不宜受。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng considered that they should not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng argued that these gifts should be declined.

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「林邑鸚鵡猶能自言苦寒，思歸其國，況二女遠別親戚乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "The Linyi parrot can still speak of its own bitter cold, longing to return to its country—how much more so two women far separated from their kin!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, "Even the Linyi parrot speaks of the bitter cold and longs to return home—how much more must these two women, torn from their families!"

sentences.zh: 並鸚鵡，各付使者而歸之。

translations.literal: Both the parrot and [the women], each was handed to the envoy and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He returned both the parrot and the women to their respective envoys for the journey home.

sentences.zh: 倭國遣使入貢，上遣新州刺史高表仁持節往撫之；

translations.literal: The Wo country sent envoys bearing tribute; the emperor dispatched Gao Biaoren, governor of Xinzhou, holding credentials to go and pacify them;
translations.idiomatic: Japan sent tribute envoys; the emperor dispatched Xinzhou Governor Gao Biaoren with imperial credentials to receive them;

sentences.zh: 表仁與其王爭禮，不宣命而還。

translations.literal: Biaoren disputed rites and protocol with their king, did not proclaim the imperial decree, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Biaoren quarreled with the Japanese king over ceremonial precedence, failed to deliver the imperial decree, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上禮圜丘。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the emperor performed rites at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor performed the rites at the Round Mound Altar.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太僕寺丞李世南開党項之地十六州、四十七縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Shinan, vice director of the Directorate of Palace Equestrian Affairs, opened up Tangut lands of sixteen prefectures and forty-seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Vice Director Li Shinan of the Palace Stud established sixteen prefectures and forty-seven counties in Tangut territory.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「朕以死刑至重，故令三覆奏，蓋欲思之詳熟故也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the attendant ministers: "I regard the death penalty as extremely weighty, and therefore ordered triple review memorials—presumably intending to consider it thoroughly and carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Because the death penalty is so serious, I instituted triple review—so that every case might be considered with due care.

sentences.zh: 而有司須臾之間，三覆已訖。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible offices, in an instant, complete all three reviews.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the officials complete all three reviews in a matter of moments.

sentences.zh: 又，古刑人，君為之徹樂減膳。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ancient times when executing criminals, the ruler would for their sake withdraw music and reduce his meals.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a criminal was executed, the ruler would stop the music and abstain from full meals.

sentences.zh: 朕庭無常設之樂，然常為之不啖酒肉，但未有著令。

translations.literal: My court has no regularly established music, yet I often for this reason do not eat meat or drink wine—only there is no fixed decree.
translations.idiomatic: My court no longer keeps music on permanent display, but I often abstain from wine and meat on execution days—though this has not yet been formally decreed.

sentences.zh: 又，百司斷獄，唯據律文，雖情在可矜，而不敢違法，其間豈能盡無冤乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, when the hundred offices pass judgment, they rely solely on the text of the law; although the circumstances may merit pity, they dare not violate the law—among them, how can there be none wrongly accused!"
translations.idiomatic: Further, officials trying cases follow the letter of the law alone. Even when mercy is warranted, they dare not bend the statute—surely innocent people are condemned along the way!

sentences.zh: 丁亥，制：「決死囚者，二日中五覆奏，下諸州者三覆奏；

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, a statute: "For deciding death-row convicts, within two days there shall be five review memorials; for those sent down to the various prefectures, three review memorials;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he issued regulations: "Death sentences in the capital shall undergo five reviews within two days; those in the provinces, three reviews;

sentences.zh: 行刑之日，尚食勿進酒肉，內教坊及太常不舉樂。

translations.literal: On the day of execution, the imperial pantry shall not serve wine or meat; the Inner Music Office and the Grand Music Office shall not perform music.
translations.idiomatic: On execution day, the imperial kitchens shall serve no wine or meat, and neither the Inner Music Office nor the Court of Imperial Sacrifices shall perform.

sentences.zh: 皆令門下覆視。

translations.literal: All shall be ordered to the Gate Department for re-review.
translations.idiomatic: All cases shall be subject to review by the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 有據法當死而情可矜者，錄狀以聞。」

translations.literal: Where according to the law one deserves death yet the circumstances merit pity, record the case and report it."
translations.idiomatic: Where the law requires death but the circumstances suggest mercy, record the details and report them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 由是全活甚眾。

translations.literal: From this a very great many were entirely spared.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, a great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 其五覆奏者，以決前一二日，至決日又三覆奏；

translations.literal: As for the five review memorials, one or two days before the decision there are [reviews], and on the day of decision there are again three review memorials;
translations.idiomatic: The five capital reviews were conducted one or two days before sentencing, with three additional reviews on execution day itself;

sentences.zh: 唯犯惡逆者一覆奏而已。

translations.literal: Only for those guilty of abominable rebellion is one review memorial sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Only offenders guilty of treason and filial impiety required a single review.

sentences.zh: 己亥，朝集使利州都督武士擭等復上表請封禪，不許。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, the Assembly Commissioners led by Lizhou Regional Commander Wu Shiwo and others again submitted a memorial requesting the Feng and Shan sacrifices; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Assembly Commissioner Wu Shiwo of Lizhou and others again petitioned for the Feng and Shan sacrifices; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: On the day renyin, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 戊申，還宮。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上謂執政曰：「朕常恐因喜怒妄行賞罰，故欲公等極諫。

translations.literal: The emperor said to those in power: "I often fear acting arbitrarily in rewards and punishments because of joy or anger, and therefore wish you to remonstrate to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "I fear letting anger or delight sway my rewards and punishments, and so I ask you to speak out without reserve.

sentences.zh: 公等亦宜受人諫，不可以己之所欲，惡人違之。

translations.literal: You also ought to accept others' remonstrance—you cannot, because of what you yourself desire, hate it when people go against you.
translations.idiomatic: You must also accept criticism yourselves. Do not resent people for opposing what you want.

sentences.zh: 苟自不能受諫，安能諫人？」

translations.literal: If you yourselves cannot accept remonstrance, how can you remonstrate with others?"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot accept advice, how can you offer it to others?

sentences.zh: 康國求內附。

translations.literal: Kangju requested to join the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju asked to submit to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「前代帝王，好招來絕域，以求服遠之名，無益於用而糜弊百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Former dynasties' emperors liked to summon and welcome distant frontier regions, seeking the reputation of subduing the far—of no use in practice yet wasting and exhausting the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Past emperors loved to draw in distant lands for the glory of ruling far-flung peoples. It served no practical purpose and only exhausted the people.

sentences.zh: 今康國內附，儻有急難，於義不得不救。

translations.literal: Now if Kangju joins the interior, if perchance there is urgent difficulty, by right one cannot but rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: If Kangju submits now and later falls into danger, we would be obliged by honor to send help.

sentences.zh: 師行萬里，豈不疲勞！

translations.literal: Armies marching ten thousand li—would they not be weary and exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: To march armies ten thousand li—what exhaustion that would mean!

sentences.zh: 勞百姓以取虛名，朕不為也。」

translations.literal: To weary the common people to obtain an empty reputation—I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: I will not burden the people for the sake of empty prestige.

sentences.zh: 遂不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore declined the offer.

sentences.zh: 謂侍臣曰：「治國如治病，病雖愈，尤宜將護，倘遽自放縱，病復作，則不可救矣。

translations.literal: He said to the attendant ministers: "Governing a state is like treating an illness—although the illness is cured, one should especially nurse and protect it; if one suddenly indulges oneself, the illness recurs, and then it cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: He told his ministers, "Governing a realm is like treating a sickness. Even after recovery, one must still guard one's health. If you relapse into excess, the illness returns—and then nothing will save you.

sentences.zh: 今中國幸安，四夷俱服，誠自古所希，然朕日慎一日，唯懼不終，故欲數聞卿輩諫爭也。」

translations.literal: Now China is fortunately at peace, the four barbarians all submit—truly rare since antiquity; yet I am cautious day by day, only fearing it will not last, and therefore wish often to hear you remonstrate and dispute."
translations.idiomatic: China is at peace and the barbarians submit—truly a rarity in history. Yet I grow more cautious daily, fearing only that this will not endure. That is why I want to hear your frank counsel again and again.

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「內外治安，臣不以為喜，唯喜陛下居安思危耳。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "That within and without are governed and at peace—I do not take it as cause for joy; I rejoice only that Your Majesty, dwelling in peace, thinks of danger."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied, "I take no joy in peace at home and abroad. I rejoice only that Your Majesty, secure in prosperity, still thinks of peril."

sentences.zh: 上嘗與侍臣論獄，魏徵曰：「煬帝時嘗有盜發，帝令於士澄捕之，少涉疑似，皆拷訊取服，凡二千餘人，帝悉令斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor once discussed criminal cases with attendant ministers; Wei Zheng said: "In Emperor Yang's time there was once a case of tomb robbing; the emperor ordered Yu Shicheng to capture [the culprits]. Those even slightly connected by suspicion were all tortured until they confessed—altogether more than two thousand people, and the emperor ordered them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing criminal justice with his ministers, Wei Zheng said, "Under Emperor Yang a tomb was robbed. Yang ordered Yu Shicheng to investigate. Anyone remotely suspected was tortured until he confessed. More than two thousand were implicated, and the emperor had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 大理丞張元濟怪其多，試尋其狀，內五人嘗為盜，餘皆平民；

translations.literal: Grand Court of Judicature Vice Director Zhang Yuanji was amazed at the number; he tried to trace their cases—among them five had formerly been thieves, the rest were all common people;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhang Yuanji of the Court of Judicial Review, astonished at the number, examined the cases and found only five former thieves among them; the rest were innocent commoners;

sentences.zh: 竟不敢執奏，盡殺之。」

translations.literal: In the end he did not dare present a memorial insisting on this, and all were killed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he dared not submit a memorial to stop it, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此豈唯煬帝無道，其臣亦不盡忠。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Was this not only Emperor Yang's lack of the Way—his ministers too did not exhaust their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This was not only Yang's depravity—his ministers failed him as well.

sentences.zh: 君臣如此，何得不亡？

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers like this—how could they not perish?
translations.idiomatic: With ruler and ministers like these, how could the dynasty survive?

sentences.zh: 公等宜戒之！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen ought to take warning from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Let this be a warning to you all!"

sentences.zh: 是歲，高州總管馮盎入朝。

translations.literal: That year, Gaozhou Regional Commander Feng Ang came to court.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Regional Commander Feng Ang of Gaozhou came to court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，羅竇諸洞獠反，敕盎帥部落二萬，為諸軍前鋒。

translations.literal: Before long, the Liao cave tribes of Luodou rebelled; an edict ordered Ang to lead twenty thousand tribal warriors as the vanguard of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Liao tribes of Luodou rebelled; the emperor ordered Feng Ang to lead twenty thousand tribal warriors as the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 獠數萬人，屯據險要，諸軍不得進。

translations.literal: The Liao numbered tens of thousands, stationed holding strategic points; the armies could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Liao warriors held the mountain passes, and the imperial forces could not advance.

sentences.zh: 盎持弩謂左右曰：「盡吾此矢，足知勝負矣。」

translations.literal: Ang took up a crossbow and said to those beside him: "Exhaust these bolts of mine, and that will suffice to know victory or defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang took up his crossbow and told his men, "Let me empty this quiver, and we will know who wins.

sentences.zh: 連發七矢，中七人。

translations.literal: He fired seven bolts in succession, hitting seven men.
translations.idiomatic: He fired seven bolts in quick succession and hit seven men.

sentences.zh: 獠皆走，因縱兵乘之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: The Liao all fled; he thereupon unleashed his troops to pursue them, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao fled; he pursued and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 上美其功，前後賞賜，不可勝數。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his achievement with rewards too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 盎所居地方二千里，奴婢萬餘人，珍貨充積；

translations.literal: The territory where Ang resided was two thousand li square; he had more than ten thousand slaves and servants, with precious goods piled in abundance;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang ruled a domain two thousand li across, with more than ten thousand retainers and storehouses overflowing with treasure;

sentences.zh: 然為治勤明，所部愛之。

translations.literal: Yet in governing he was diligent and clear; those under his jurisdiction loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he governed diligently and wisely, and his people adored him.

sentences.zh: 新羅王真平卒，無嗣，國人立其女善德為王。

translations.literal: King Jinpyeong of Silla died; having no heir, the people of the state installed his daughter Seondeok as king.
translations.idiomatic: King Jinpyeong of Silla died without an heir; the Silla people enthroned his daughter, Queen Seondeok.
